sentences.zh: 【唐紀七十五】 起玄黓困敦，盡閼逢攝提格，凡三年。

translations.literal: [Tang Records 75] From Xuanyi Kundun through Efeng Shetige; three years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records 75] From Xuanyi Kundun through Efeng Shetige—three years in all.

sentences.zh: 昭宗聖穆景文孝皇帝上之中景福元年（

translations.literal: First year of the Jingfu era of Emperor Zhaozong, the Sagacious, Reverent, Cultivated, and Filial, upper fascicle, middle section (
translations.idiomatic: First year of the Jingfu era of Emperor Zhaozong (upper fascicle, middle section) (

sentences.zh: 壬子，公元八九二年）

translations.literal: rensi, corresponding to the year 892 CE)
translations.idiomatic: the year rensi, equivalent to 892 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丙寅，赦天下，改元。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day bingyin, a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm and the era name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the day bingyin, the court proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔李茂貞、靜難王行瑜、鎮國韓建、同州王行約、秦州李茂莊五節度使上言：楊守亮容匿叛臣復恭，請出軍討之，乞加茂貞山南西道詔討使。

translations.literal: The five military governors Li Maozhen of Fengxiang, Wang Xingyu of Jingnan, Han Jian of Zhenguo, Wang Xingyue of Tongzhou, and Li Maozhuang of Qinzhou submitted a joint memorial stating that Yang Shouliang was harboring the rebel minister Zhang Fugong and requesting permission to send troops to punish him; they asked that Maozhen be appointed Pacification Commissioner for the Shannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Li Maozhen of Fengxiang, Wang Xingyu of Jingnan, Han Jian of Zhenguo, Wang Xingyue of Tongzhou, and Li Maozhuang of Qinzhou—the five circuit governors—jointly memorialized that Yang Shouliang was sheltering the rebel Zhang Fugong and asked to march against him, requesting that Maozhen be made Pacification Commissioner for Shannan West.

sentences.zh: 朝議以茂貞得山南，不可複製，下詔和解之，皆不聽。

translations.literal: The court debated that if Maozhen obtained Shannan, he could not be controlled again; an edict was issued to reconcile the matter, but none of them obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: The court feared that once Maozhen held Shannan he could never be restrained again and issued an edict seeking a settlement, but all five refused to comply.

sentences.zh: 王鎔、李匡威合兵十餘萬攻堯山，李克用遣其將李嗣勳擊之，大破幽、鎮兵，斬獲三萬。

translations.literal: Wang Rong and Li Kuangwei combined their forces, more than a hundred thousand strong, to attack Yaoshan. Li Keyong dispatched his general Li Sixun to strike them and routed the Youzhou and Zhenzhou armies, killing and capturing thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong and Li Kuangwei joined forces—more than a hundred thousand men—to attack Yaoshan. Li Keyong sent his general Li Sixun against them and shattered the Youzhou and Zhenzhou troops, killing or capturing thirty thousand.

sentences.zh: 楊行密謂諸將曰：「孫儒之眾十倍於我，吾戰數不利，欲退保銅官，何如？」

translations.literal: Yang Xingmi said to his generals: "Sun Ru's forces are ten times ours. We have been defeated repeatedly in battle and wish to withdraw and hold Tongguan—what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi asked his commanders, "Sun Ru outnumbers us tenfold. We've lost fight after fight. I'm thinking of falling back to Tongguan—what do you say?"

sentences.zh: 劉威、李神福曰：「儒掃地遠來，利在速戰。

translations.literal: Liu Wei and Li Shenfu said: "Ru has swept across the land to come from afar; his advantage lies in swift battle.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wei and Li Shenfu replied, "Sun Ru has marched clean across the country to get here—he needs a quick fight.

sentences.zh: 宜屯據險要，堅壁清野以老其師，時出輕騎抄其饋餉，奪其俘掠。

translations.literal: We should hold strong defensive positions, fortify the walls and clear the countryside to wear down his army, and from time to time send light cavalry to raid his supply lines and seize what his men have plundered.
translations.idiomatic: We should hold the defiles, strengthen the walls, and strip the countryside bare to exhaust his army, while sending out light horse now and then to cut his supplies and seize his booty.

sentences.zh: 彼前不得戰，退無資糧，可坐擒也。」

translations.literal: If they cannot fight ahead and have no provisions when they retreat, we can take them without a struggle."
translations.idiomatic: Blocked from attacking and starved on the retreat, he'll be ours for the taking."

sentences.zh: 戴友規曰：「儒與我相持數年，勝負略相當。

translations.literal: Dai Yougui said: "Ru and we have faced each other for several years, with victories and defeats roughly equal.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yougui said, "Sun Ru and we have traded blows for years—wins and losses about even.

sentences.zh: 今悉眾致死於我，我若望風棄城，正墮其計。

translations.literal: Now he has brought his entire host to fight us to the death. If we abandon our cities at the first sign of pressure, we will fall right into his trap.
translations.idiomatic: Now he's thrown everything at us. If we flee at the first alarm, we play straight into his hands.

sentences.zh: 淮南士民從公渡江及自儒來降者甚，公宜遣將先護送歸淮南，使復生業，儒軍聞淮南安堵，皆有思歸之心，人心既搖，安得不敗！」

translations.literal: Many people of Huainan who crossed the river with you and many who surrendered from Ru's side—Your Lordship should dispatch generals to escort them back to Huainan first and let them resume their livelihoods. When Ru's army hears that Huainan is secure, all will yearn to return home. Once morale wavers, how can they fail to be defeated!"
translations.idiomatic: Countless Huainan civilians followed you across the Yangtze, and many have defected from Sun Ru. Send officers to escort them home and restore their livelihoods. When Sun Ru's troops hear Huainan is at peace, they'll pine for home. Once hearts turn, how can he stand?"

sentences.zh: 行密悅，從之。

translations.literal: Xingmi was pleased and followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi was delighted and did as he advised.

sentences.zh: 友規，廬州人也。

translations.literal: Yougui was a native of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yougui was from Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 威戎節度使楊晟與楊守亮等約攻王建，二月，丁丑，晟出兵掠新繁、漢州之境，使其將呂堯將兵二千會楊守厚攻梓州；

translations.literal: Yang Sheng, military governor of Weirong, agreed with Yang Shouliang and others to attack Wang Jian. In the second month, on the day dingchou, Sheng marched out to raid the borders of Xinfan and Hanzhou, and sent his general Lü Yao with two thousand troops to join Yang Shouhou in attacking Zizhou;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sheng of Weirong joined Yang Shouliang and others in a pact to strike Wang Jian. In the second month, on dingchou, Sheng raided Xinfan and Hanzhou and sent Lü Yao with two thousand men to link up with Yang Shouhou's assault on Zizhou;

sentences.zh: 建遣行營都指揮使李簡擊堯，斬之。

translations.literal: Jian dispatched his campaign chief Li Jian to attack Yao and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian sent his field commander Li Jian against Lü Yao and had him killed.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，朱全忠出兵擊朱瑄，遣其子友裕將兵前行，軍於斗門。

translations.literal: On the day wuyin, Zhu Quanzhong marched out to attack Zhu Xuan, sending his son Youyu ahead in command of the vanguard, encamping at Doumen.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, Zhu Quanzhong marched against Zhu Xuan, sending his son Youyu ahead with the vanguard to camp at Doumen.

sentences.zh: 李茂貞、王行瑜擅舉兵擊興元。

translations.literal: Li Maozhen and Wang Xingyu took it upon themselves to raise troops and attack Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Maozhen and Wang Xingyu marched on Xingyuan without imperial authorization.

sentences.zh: 茂貞表求招討使不已，遺杜讓能、西門君遂書，陵蔑朝廷。

translations.literal: Maozhen repeatedly memorialized requesting appointment as Pacification Commissioner, and sent letters to Du Rangneng and Ximen Junsui, treating the court with contempt.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen kept petitioning for the pacification commission and wrote Du Rangneng and Ximen Junsui with open contempt for the throne.

sentences.zh: 上意不能容，御延英，召宰相、諫官議之。

translations.literal: The emperor could not tolerate this. He held court in the Yanying Hall and summoned the chief ministers and remonstrance officials to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's patience was exhausted. He convened the Yanying Hall, calling in the chief ministers and censors to debate the matter.

sentences.zh: 時宦官有陰與二鎮相表裡者，宰相相顧不敢言，上不悅。

translations.literal: At the time some eunuchs were secretly in league with the two circuits; the chief ministers looked at one another and dared not speak, and the emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Some eunuchs were secretly backing the two warlords. The chief ministers exchanged glances and held their tongues, which displeased the emperor.

sentences.zh: 給事中牛徽曰：「先朝多難，茂貞誠有翼衛之功；

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Niu Hui said: "The previous reign endured many calamities, and Maozhen truly rendered meritorious service in guarding and protecting the throne;
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Niu Hui said, "The late reign knew endless troubles, and Maozhen did help shield the throne—

sentences.zh: 諸楊阻兵，亟出攻討，其志亦在疾惡，但不當不俟詔命耳。

translations.literal: the various Yangs are blocking the roads with armed force, and he has urgently marched out to attack and punish them. His intent is likewise to abhor evil, but he ought not to have acted without awaiting an imperial command.
translations.idiomatic: the Yang clan are in armed rebellion, and he rushed out to strike them—his heart is in the right place, but he should not have moved without an imperial order.

sentences.zh: 比聞兵過山南，殺傷至多。

translations.literal: Recently I have heard that as his troops passed through Shannan, the killing and wounding were extremely numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Word is his army ravaged Shannan, killing and wounding without count.

sentences.zh: 陛下倘不以招討使授之，使用國法約束，則山南之民盡矣。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty will not grant him the post of Pacification Commissioner but instead employ the laws of the state to restrain him, then the people of Shannan will be utterly destroyed."
translations.idiomatic: If you withhold the pacification commission and bind him with the law instead, the people of Shannan may yet be saved."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「此言是也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "These words are correct."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "He is right."

sentences.zh: 乃以茂貞為山南西道招討使。

translations.literal: Then Maozhen was appointed Pacification Commissioner for the Shannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen was then made Pacification Commissioner for Shannan West.

sentences.zh: 甲申，朱全忠至衛南，朱瑄將步騎萬人襲斗門，朱友裕棄營走，瑄據其營。

translations.literal: On the day jiashen, Zhu Quanzhong reached Weinan. Zhu Xuan led ten thousand infantry and cavalry in a surprise attack on Doumen; Zhu Youyu abandoned the camp and fled, and Xuan seized it.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, Zhu Quanzhong reached Weinan. Zhu Xuan struck Doumen with ten thousand horse and foot; Zhu Youyu fled and Xuan took the camp.

sentences.zh: 全忠不知，乙酉，引兵趣斗門，至者皆為鄆人所殺。

translations.literal: Quanzhong did not know. On the day yiyou he led troops toward Doumen; all who arrived were killed by the men of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong knew nothing of this. On yiyou he marched for Doumen; every man who reached it was cut down by Yan troops.

sentences.zh: 全忠退軍瓠河，丁亥，瑄擊全忠，大破之，全忠走。

translations.literal: Quanzhong withdrew his army to Hulu River. On the day dinghai, Xuan attacked Quanzhong and routed him utterly; Quanzhong fled.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong fell back to the Hulu River. On dinghai, Xuan smashed his army and Quanzhong ran.

sentences.zh: 張歸厚於後力戰，全忠僅免，副使李璠等皆死。

translations.literal: Zhang Guihou fought desperately in the rear; Quanzhong barely escaped, while Vice Commissioner Li Fan and others all perished.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guihou fought a rear-guard action and Quanzhong barely got away; Vice Commissioner Li Fan and others were killed.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠奏貶河陽節度使趙克裕，以佑國節度使張全義兼河陽節度使。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong memorialized that the military governor of Heyang, Zhao Keyu, be demoted, and that Zhang Quanyi, military governor of Youguo, be appointed concurrently as military governor of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong had Heyang governor Zhao Keyu demoted and made Youguo governor Zhang Quanyi also hold Heyang.

sentences.zh: 孫儒圍宣州。

translations.literal: Sun Ru besieged Xuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ru laid siege to Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，劉建鋒為孫儒守常州，將兵從儒擊楊行密，甘露鎮使陳可言帥部兵千人據常州。

translations.literal: Earlier, Liu Jianfeng had garrisoned Changzhou for Sun Ru and marched with Ru to attack Yang Xingmi. Chen Keran, commissioner of Ganlu Town, led a thousand troops of his command to hold Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jianfeng had been left to hold Changzhou for Sun Ru while Ru marched against Yang Xingmi. Chen Keran of Ganlu Town held the city with a thousand men.

sentences.zh: 行密將張訓引兵奄至城下，可言倉猝出迎，訓手刃殺之，遂取常州。

translations.literal: Yang Xingmi's general Zhang Xun led troops that suddenly appeared below the walls. Keran rushed out in haste to meet them; Xun killed him with his own hand and then took Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun of Yang Xingmi's command appeared suddenly at the walls. Keran rushed out to meet him; Xun cut him down himself and seized Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 行密別將又取潤州。

translations.literal: Another of Xingmi's generals also captured Runzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Another of Xingmi's commanders took Runzhou as well.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠連年攻時溥，塗、泗、濠三州民不得耕獲，袞、兗、河東兵救之，皆無功，復值水災，人死者什六七。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong had attacked Shi Pu year after year. The people of the three prefectures of Tu, Si, and Hao could not plow or harvest. Troops from Yan, Yanzhou, and Hedong came to his aid, all without success; moreover there was flooding, and six or seven tenths of the people died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong had besieged Shi Pu for years. In Tu, Si, and Hao the people could neither sow nor reap. Armies from Yan, Yanzhou, and Hedong marched to relieve him, all in vain; floods followed, and six or seven people in ten perished.

sentences.zh: 溥困甚，請和於全忠，全忠曰：「必移鎮乃可。」

translations.literal: Pu was in desperate straits and sought peace with Quanzhong. Quanzhong said: "You must transfer to another circuit—only then is it possible."
translations.idiomatic: Pu was desperate and sued for peace. Quanzhong said, "You must accept transfer to another post—that's the only way."

sentences.zh: 溥許之。

translations.literal: Pu agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Pu agreed.

sentences.zh: 全忠乃奏請移溥它鎮，仍命大臣鎮徐州。

translations.literal: Quanzhong then memorialized requesting that Pu be moved to another circuit and that a senior minister be appointed to govern Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong memorialized to move Pu elsewhere and station a senior minister at Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 詔以門下侍郎、同平章事劉崇望同平章事，充感化節度使，以溥為太子太師。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Chief Minister Liu Chongwang as Associate Chief Minister and military governor of Ganhua, and made Pu Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The court named Liu Chongwang, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Chief Minister, military governor of Ganhua, and made Pu Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 溥恐全忠詐而殺之，據城不奉詔，崇望及華陰而還。

translations.literal: Pu feared that Quanzhong was deceiving him and would kill him; he held the city and refused to obey the edict. Chongwang reached Huayin and turned back.
translations.idiomatic: Pu feared a trap and refused the edict, holding the city. Chongwang got as far as Huayin and turned back.

sentences.zh: 忠義節度使趙德諲薨，子匡凝代之。

translations.literal: Zhao Dexin, military governor of Zhongyi, died; his son Kuangning succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Dexin of Zhongyi died; his son Kuangning replaced him.

sentences.zh: 范暉驕侈失眾心，王潮以從弟彥復為都統，弟審知為都監，將兵攻福州。

translations.literal: Fan Hui was arrogant and extravagant and lost the hearts of the people. Wang Chao appointed his cousin Yanfu as supreme commander and his younger brother Shenzhi as chief overseer, and led troops to attack Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Hui's arrogance cost him the people's loyalty. Wang Chao made his cousin Yanfu supreme commander and his brother Shenzhi chief overseer, and marched on Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 民自請輸米餉軍，平湖洞及濱海蠻夷皆以兵船助之。

translations.literal: The people volunteered to supply grain to feed the army; the Pinghu cave people and the coastal barbarians all aided with warships.
translations.idiomatic: Civilians volunteered grain for the army; the Pinghu cave folk and coastal tribes sent war junks to help.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，王建遣族子嘉州刺史宗裕、雅州刺史王宗侃、威信都指揮使華洪、茂州刺史王宗瑤將兵五萬攻彭州，楊晟逆戰而敗，宗裕等圍之。

translations.literal: On the day xinchou, Wang Jian dispatched his clansmen—the prefect of Jiazhou, Zongyu; the prefect of Yazhou, Wang Zongkan; the director of Weixin Command, Hua Hong; and the prefect of Maozhou, Wang Zongyao—to lead fifty thousand troops against Pengzhou. Yang Sheng met them in battle and was defeated; Zongyu and the others besieged the city.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, Wang Jian sent fifty thousand men under his kinsmen Zongyu of Jiazhou, Zongkan of Yazhou, Hua Hong of Weixin Command, and Zongyao of Maozhou against Pengzhou. Yang Sheng was beaten in the field and the city was invested.

sentences.zh: 楊守亮遣其將符昭救晟，逕趨成都，營三學山。

translations.literal: Yang Shouliang sent his general Fu Zhao to rescue Sheng. Zhao marched straight for Chengdu and encamped on Mount Sanxue.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shouliang sent Fu Zhao to relieve Sheng. Zhao struck straight for Chengdu and camped on Mount Sanxue.

sentences.zh: 建亟召華洪還。

translations.literal: Jian urgently recalled Hua Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Jian urgently recalled Hua Hong.

sentences.zh: 洪疾驅而至，後軍尚未集，以數百人夜去昭營數里，多擊更鼓；

translations.literal: Hong raced there at speed. His rear guard had not yet assembled; with several hundred men he went by night several li from Zhao's camp and beat the night watches in many places;
translations.idiomatic: Hong galloped back. His rear had not yet come up; with a few hundred men he stole several li from Zhao's camp by night and beat watch-drums in many places;

sentences.zh: 昭以為蜀軍大至，引兵宵遁。

translations.literal: Zhao thought a great Shu army had arrived and withdrew his troops by night.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao thought the whole Shu army was upon him and fled by night.

sentences.zh: 三月，以戶部尚書鄭延昌為中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: In the third month, Zheng Yanchang, Minister of Revenue, was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Revenue Minister Zheng Yanchang was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Chief Minister.

sentences.zh: 延昌，從讜之從兄弟也。

translations.literal: Yanchang was a cousin of Zheng Congdang.
translations.idiomatic: Yanchang was Zheng Congdang's cousin.

sentences.zh: 左神策勇勝三都都指揮使楊子實、子遷、子釗，皆守亮之假子也，自渠州引兵救楊晟，知守亮必敗，壬子，帥其眾二萬降於王建。

translations.literal: Yang Zishi, Yang Ziqian, and Yang Zizhao, commanders of the three Left Divine Strategy Brave Victory commands, were all Shouliang's adopted sons. They led troops from Qizhou to rescue Yang Sheng; knowing Shouliang was doomed, on the day renzi they brought their twenty thousand followers and surrendered to Wang Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zishi, Ziqian, and Zizhao of the Left Divine Strategy Brave Victory commands—all Shouliang's adopted sons—marched from Qizhou to save Yang Sheng. Seeing defeat coming, on renzi they surrendered twenty thousand men to Wang Jian.

sentences.zh: 李克用、王處存合兵攻王鎔，癸丑，拔天長鎮。

translations.literal: Li Keyong and Wang Chucun combined forces to attack Wang Rong. On the day guichou they captured Tianchang Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong and Wang Chucun joined against Wang Rong and on guichou took Tianchang Fort.

sentences.zh: 戊午，鎔與戰於新市，大破之，殺獲三萬餘人；

translations.literal: On the day wuwu, Rong fought them at Xinshi and routed them utterly, killing and capturing more than thirty thousand;
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, Rong met them at Xinshi and shattered them, killing or capturing more than thirty thousand;

sentences.zh: 辛酉，克用退屯欒城。

translations.literal: on the day xinyou, Keyong withdrew and encamped at Luancheng.
translations.idiomatic: on xinyou Keyong fell back to Luancheng.

sentences.zh: 詔和解河東及鎮、定、幽四鎮。

translations.literal: An edict ordered reconciliation among Hedong and the four circuits of Zhen, Ding, and You.
translations.idiomatic: An edict commanded peace among Hedong, Zhen, Ding, and You.

sentences.zh: 楊晟遺楊守貞、楊守忠、楊守厚書，使攻東川以解彭州之圍，守貞等從之。

translations.literal: Yang Sheng sent letters to Yang Shouzhen, Yang Shouzhong, and Yang Shouhou, ordering them to attack Dongchuan to relieve the siege of Pengzhou; Shouzhen and the others obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sheng wrote Yang Shouzhen, Shouzhong, and Shouhou to strike Dongchuan and lift the siege of Pengzhou; they complied.

sentences.zh: 神策督將竇行實戍梓州，守厚密誘之為內應；

translations.literal: The Divine Strategy supervising general Dou Xingshi was garrisoned at Zizhou; Shouhou secretly induced him to act as an inside collaborator;
translations.idiomatic: Dou Xingshi of the Divine Strategy garrisoned Zizhou; Shouhou secretly won him as an inside man;

sentences.zh: 守厚至涪城，行實事洩，顧彥暉斬之。

translations.literal: when Shouhou reached Fucheng, Xingshi's plot was exposed and Gu Yanhui beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: but when Shouhou reached Fucheng the plot leaked and Gu Yanhui executed Xingshi.

sentences.zh: 守厚遁去。

translations.literal: Shouhou fled.
translations.idiomatic: Shouhou fled.

sentences.zh: 守貞、守忠軍至，無所歸，盤桓綿、劍間，王建遣其將吉諫襲守厚，破之。

translations.literal: Shouzhen and Shouzhong's armies arrived but had nowhere to go and lingered between Mian and Jian. Wang Jian sent his general Ji Jian to strike Shouhou and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhen and Shouzhong arrived with nowhere to go and wandered between Mian and Jian. Wang Jian sent Ji Jian against Shouhou and broke him.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，西川將李簡邀擊守忠於鐘陽，斬獲三千餘人。

translations.literal: On the day guihai, the Shu general Li Jian intercepted Shouzhong at Zhongyang and killed or captured more than three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, Li Jian of Shu ambushed Shouzhong at Zhongyang and killed or captured over three thousand.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，簡又破守厚於銅鉾，斬獲三千餘人，降萬五千人；

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Jian again defeated Shouhou at Tongzhen, killing and capturing more than three thousand and accepting the surrender of fifteen thousand;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, Jian again routed Shouhou at Tongzhen, killing or capturing three thousand and taking fifteen thousand prisoners;

sentences.zh: 守忠、守厚皆走。

translations.literal: Shouzhong and Shouhou both fled.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhong and Shouhou both fled.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，置武勝軍於杭州，以錢鏐為防禦使。

translations.literal: On the day yiyou, the Wusheng Army was established at Hangzhou, and Qian Liu was appointed Defense Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou the Wusheng Army was set up at Hangzhou and Qian Liu made Defense Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 天威軍使賈德晟，以李順節之死，頗怨憤，西門君遂惡之，奏而殺之。

translations.literal: Jia Desheng, commissioner of the Tianwei Army, was deeply resentful over Li Shunjie's death. Ximen Junsui hated him and memorialized for his execution; he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Desheng of the Tianwei Army nursed bitter grievance over Li Shunjie's death. Ximen Junsui turned on him and had him executed by memorial.

sentences.zh: 德晟麾下千餘騎奔鳳翔，李茂貞由是益強。

translations.literal: More than a thousand horsemen of Desheng's command fled to Fengxiang, and Li Maozhen thereby grew stronger still.
translations.idiomatic: Over a thousand of his horsemen fled to Fengxiang, and Li Maozhen grew stronger still.

sentences.zh: 李匡威出兵侵雲、代，壬寅，李克用始引兵還。

translations.literal: Li Kuangwei marched out to invade Yun and Dai. On the day renyin, Li Keyong at last led his troops back.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kuangwei invaded Yun and Dai. On renyin, Li Keyong finally marched home.

sentences.zh: 時溥遣兵南侵，至楚州，楊行密將張訓、李德誠敗之於壽河，遂取楚州，執其刺史劉瓚。

translations.literal: Shi Pu dispatched troops south in invasion as far as Chuzhou. Yang Xingmi's generals Zhang Xun and Li Decheng defeated them at the Shou River, then took Chuzhou and seized its prefect Liu Zan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Pu sent troops south to Chuzhou. Zhang Xun and Li Decheng of Yang Xingmi's command beat them at the Shou River, took Chuzhou, and seized Prefect Liu Zan.

sentences.zh: 五月，加邠寧節度使王行瑜兼中書令。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Wang Xingyu, military governor of Binning, was given the additional title of Chief Minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Binning governor Wang Xingyu was also made Chief Minister of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 楊行密屢敗孫儒兵，破其廣德營，張訓屯安吉，斷其糧道。

translations.literal: Yang Xingmi repeatedly defeated Sun Ru's forces, destroyed his Guangde camp, and had Zhang Xun encamp at Anji, cutting his supply route.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi beat Sun Ru again and again, smashed his Guangde camp, and posted Zhang Xun at Anji to sever his supplies.

sentences.zh: 儒食盡，士卒大疫，遣其將劉建鋒、馬殷分兵掠諸縣。

translations.literal: Ru ran out of food; his soldiers suffered a great pestilence. He sent his generals Liu Jianfeng and Ma Yin to divide their forces and plunder the various counties.
translations.idiomatic: Ru starved; plague swept his ranks. He sent Liu Jianfeng and Ma Yin to plunder the counties for food.

sentences.zh: 六月，行密聞儒疾瘧，戊寅，縱兵擊之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Xingmi heard that Ru was ill with malaria. On the day wuyin he unleashed his troops to attack.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, hearing Ru had malaria, Xingmi on wuyin threw his whole army at him.

sentences.zh: 會大雨、晦冥，儒軍大敗，安仁義破儒五十餘寨，田頵擒儒於陳，斬之，傳首京師，儒眾多降於行密。

translations.literal: A great rain fell and the sky grew dark. Ru's army was utterly defeated. An Renyi destroyed more than fifty of Ru's stockades. Tian Jun captured Ru in battle, beheaded him, and sent his head to the capital; most of Ru's followers surrendered to Xingmi.
translations.idiomatic: Rain fell in torrents and the day went black. Ru's army collapsed. An Renyi stormed fifty of his camps. Tian Jun seized Ru in the press of battle, beheaded him, and sent his head to the capital; most of Ru's men surrendered to Xingmi.

sentences.zh: 劉建鋒、馬殷收餘眾七千，南走洪州，推建鋒為帥，殷為先鋒指揮使，以行軍司馬張佶為謀主，比至江西，眾十餘萬。

translations.literal: Liu Jianfeng and Ma Yin gathered the remaining seven thousand and fled south to Hongzhou. They made Jianfeng commander, Yin vanguard commander, and their campaign secretary Zhang Ji chief strategist. By the time they reached Jiangxi, their force exceeded a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jianfeng and Ma Yin rallied seven thousand survivors and fled south to Hongzhou. They made Jianfeng commander, Yin vanguard commander, and Zhang Ji their strategist. By Jiangxi their host had swelled past a hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，楊行密帥眾歸揚州；

translations.literal: On the day dingyou, Yang Xingmi led his host back to Yangzhou;
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, Yang Xingmi marched his army home to Yangzhou;

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丙辰，至廣陵，表田頵守宣州，安仁義守潤州。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day bingchen, he reached Guangling and memorialized that Tian Jun hold Xuanzhou and An Renyi hold Runzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on bingchen he reached Guangling and recommended Tian Jun for Xuanzhou and An Renyi for Runzhou.

sentences.zh: 先是，揚州富庶甲天下，時人稱揚一、益二，及經秦、畢、孫、楊兵火之餘，江、淮之間，東西千里掃地盡矣。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yangzhou's wealth had led all under heaven; people said "Yangzhou first, Yizhou second." After passing through the fires of war under Qin, Bi, Sun, and Yang, between the Jiang and the Huai, for a thousand li east and west, the land was swept utterly bare.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yangzhou's riches led the empire—"first Yangzhou, second Yizhou," men said. After the wars of Qin, Bi, Sun, and Yang, the Jiang-Huai corridor for a thousand li east and west lay utterly waste.

sentences.zh: 王建圍彭州，久不下，民皆竄匿山谷；

translations.literal: Wang Jian besieged Pengzhou but could not take it for a long time; the people all fled and hid in the mountains and valleys;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian besieged Pengzhou for months without success; the people hid in the hills;

sentences.zh: 諸寨日出俘掠，謂之「淘虜」，都將先擇其善者，餘則士卒分之，以是為常。

translations.literal: each day the stockades sent men out to seize captives in raids called "sifting for captives." The commanders first chose the best for themselves; the rest the soldiers divided among themselves—this became routine.
translations.idiomatic: Every day the camps sent men out on "sifting" raids for captives. Commanders took the pick; soldiers split the rest—this was daily custom.

sentences.zh: 有軍士王先成者，新津人，本書生也，世亂，為兵，度諸將惟北寨王宗侃最賢，乃往說之曰：「彭州本西川之巡屬也，陳、田召楊晟，割四州以授之，偽署觀察使，與之共拒朝命。

translations.literal: There was a soldier named Wang Xiancheng, a native of Xinjin, originally a scholar. In the chaos of the age he became a soldier. Judging among the generals that Wang Zongkan of the northern stockade alone was the most worthy, he went to persuade him, saying: "Pengzhou was originally a subordinate prefecture of Xichuan. Chen and Tian summoned Yang Sheng, ceded four prefectures to invest him, and falsely appointed him military commissioner, joining with him to resist the court's command.
translations.idiomatic: A soldier named Wang Xiancheng, from Xinjin, had been a scholar before the wars made him a fighting man. He reckoned Wang Zongkan of the northern camp the best of the commanders and went to him, saying, "Pengzhou was always part of Xichuan. Chen and Tian brought in Yang Sheng, gave him four prefectures, and set him up as commissioner to defy the throne.

sentences.zh: 今陳、田已平而晟猶據之，州民皆知西川乃其大府而司徒乃其主也，故大軍始至，民不入城而入同谷避之，以俟招安。

translations.literal: Now Chen and Tian have been pacified yet Sheng still holds it. The people of the prefecture all know that Xichuan is their great government seat and that the Minister of Works is their lord. Therefore when the great army first arrived, the people did not enter the city but went into Tonggu to take refuge, waiting to be brought to submission.
translations.idiomatic: Chen and Tian are gone but Sheng still holds the city. The people know Xichuan is their capital and you are their lord. When your army came they fled to Tonggu, waiting to surrender.

sentences.zh: 今軍至累月，未聞招安之命，軍士復從而掠之，與盜賊無異，奪其資財，驅其畜產，分其老弱婦女以為奴婢，使父子兄弟流離愁怨；

translations.literal: The army has been here for months, yet no order of amnesty has been heard. The soldiers again follow in plundering them, no different from bandits—seizing their goods, driving off their livestock, dividing their old, weak, and women as slaves and servants, so that fathers and sons and brothers are scattered in sorrow and resentment;
translations.idiomatic: Your men have been here for months with no word of amnesty. They plunder like bandits—seizing goods, driving off livestock, taking the old and women as slaves—scattering families in grief and rage;

sentences.zh: 其在山中者暴露於暑雨，殘傷於蛇虎，孤危飢渴，無所歸訴。

translations.literal: those in the mountains are exposed to summer heat and rain, maimed by snakes and tigers, lonely, desperate, hungry and thirsty, with nowhere to turn for redress.
translations.idiomatic: Those in the hills suffer heat and rain, snakes and tigers; they are hungry, helpless, with nowhere to turn.

sentences.zh: 彼始以楊晟非其主而不從，今司徒不加存恤，彼更思楊氏矣。」

translations.literal: They first refused to follow because Yang Sheng was not their lord. Now if the Minister of Works does not show them care and relief, they will think of the Yang clan again."
translations.idiomatic: They rejected Yang Sheng because he was not their lord. If you show no mercy, they will long for the Yangs again."

sentences.zh: 宗侃惻然，不覺屢移其床前問之，先成曰：「又有甚於是者，今諸寨每旦出六七百人，入山淘虜，薄暮乃返，曾無守備之意，賴城中無人耳，萬一有智者為之畫策，使乘虛奔突，先伏精兵千人於門內，登城望淘虜者稍遠，出弓弩手、砲手各百人，攻寨之一面，隨以役卒五百，負薪土填壕為道，然後出精兵奮擊，且焚其寨；

translations.literal: Zongkan was moved to compassion and, without noticing, shifted his seat forward again and again to question him. Xiancheng said: "There is something worse still. Now each day every stockade sends out six or seven hundred men into the mountains to sift for captives and returns only at dusk, utterly without thought of defense—relying solely on there being no one in the city. Should some clever man devise a plan, sending men to burst in while the camps are empty, first hiding a thousand elite troops inside the gates, mounting the walls to watch until the sifters are far off, then sending out a hundred archers and a hundred artillerymen to attack one face of a stockade, followed by five hundred laborers bearing brush and earth to fill the moat and make a path, and then sending elite troops to strike fiercely and burn the stockade;
translations.idiomatic: Zongkan was moved and leaned forward again and again to hear him out. Xiancheng said, "It is worse than that. Every camp sends six or seven hundred men out each dawn to sift the hills for captives and does not return until dusk, with no thought of defense—only because the city is empty. If a clever enemy struck while the camps were bare—hid a thousand picked men in the gates, waited until the raiders were far off, sent out archers and catapult crews to storm one face, followed by five hundred laborers with brush and earth to fill the moat, then elite troops to burn the camp—

sentences.zh: 又於三面城下各出耀兵，諸寨鹹自備御，無暇相救，城中得以益兵繼出，如此，能無敗乎！」

translations.literal: and at the same time displaying troops below the walls on three sides so that every stockade would be busy defending itself and have no leisure to rescue another, while the city could keep sending out reinforcements—in such fashion, how could there be no defeat!"
translations.idiomatic: and showed troops before the walls on three sides so every camp would defend itself and none could help another, while the city poured out more men—in such a case, how could you not be ruined?"

sentences.zh: 宗侃矍然曰：「此誠有之，將若之何？」

translations.literal: Zongkan started in alarm and said: "This is truly so—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Zongkan started. "You are right—what can we do?"

sentences.zh: 先成請條列為狀以白王建，宗侃即命先成草之，大指言：「今所白之事，須四面通共，宗侃所司止於北面，或所白可從，乞以牙舉施行。」

translations.literal: Xiancheng asked to set the points out in a memorial to report to Wang Jian. Zongkan at once ordered Xiancheng to draft it. The main import was: "What is now reported must be shared on all four sides. Zongkan's responsibility extends only to the north face. If what is reported may be adopted, I beg that it be submitted through the headquarters staff for implementation."
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng asked to draft a memorial to Wang Jian. Zongkan had him write it at once. Its gist: "These matters must be shared on all four sides. I command only the north. If the Prince approves, let headquarters issue the orders."

sentences.zh: 事凡七條：「其一，乞招安山中百姓。

translations.literal: The matters totaled seven articles: "First, I beg to bring the mountain people to submission.
translations.idiomatic: There were seven points: "First, bring the mountain people in.

sentences.zh: 其二，乞禁諸寨軍士及子弟無得一人輒出淘虜，仍表諸寨之旁七里內聽樵牧，敢越表者斬。

translations.literal: Second, I beg to forbid soldiers and their dependents in every stockade from going out to sift for captives on their own; moreover, mark out seven li around each stockade where fuel-gathering and grazing are permitted—whoever crosses the mark is to be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Second, forbid any soldier or dependent to go out sifting for captives; mark seven li around each camp for wood and grazing—cross the line and die.

sentences.zh: 其三，乞置招安寨，中容數千人，以處所招百姓，宗侃請選所部將校謹干者為招安將，使將三十人晝夜執兵巡衛。

translations.literal: Third, I beg to establish a submission stockade large enough for several thousand to house those brought in. Zongkan asks to select capable and diligent officers from his command as submission commissioners, each with thirty men to bear arms and patrol day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Third, set up a submission camp for several thousand. Zongkan will choose steady officers as submission commissioners, each with thirty armed men to patrol day and night.

sentences.zh: 其四，招安之事須委一人總領，今榜帖既下，諸寨必各遣軍士入山招安，百姓見之無不驚疑，如鼠見狸，誰肯來者！

translations.literal: Fourth, the work of submission must be entrusted to one person in overall charge. Now that placards have been posted, every stockade is sure to send soldiers into the mountains to bring people in. When the people see them, none fail to be alarmed and suspicious—as mice at the sight of a cat—who would be willing to come!
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, one man must oversee submission. With placards posted, every camp will send men into the hills; the people will flee like mice from a cat—who will come in?

sentences.zh: 欲招之必有其術，願降帖付宗侃專掌其事。

translations.literal: To bring them in there must be a method. I beg that an edict be issued placing the matter solely in Zongkan's hands.
translations.idiomatic: There is a right way to win them. Issue an order putting Zongkan solely in charge.

sentences.zh: 其五，乞嚴勒四寨指揮使，悉索前日所虜彭州男女老幼集於營場，有父子、兄弟、夫婦自相認者即使相從，牒其人數，部送招安寨，有敢私匿一人者斬；

translations.literal: Fifth, I beg to strictly order the four stockade commanders to gather all the men, women, old, and young of Pengzhou seized in recent days at the drill ground. Where father and son, brother and brother, or husband and wife recognize one another, let them go together. Register their numbers and escort them to the submission stockade. Whoever dares hide a single person privately is to be beheaded;
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, order the four camp commanders to assemble every Pengzhou captive at the drill ground. Let kin recognize kin and go together. Register them and send them to the submission camp. Hide one person and die;

sentences.zh: 仍乞勒府中諸營，亦令嚴索，有自軍前先寄歸者，量給資糧，悉部送歸招安寨。

translations.literal: Still I beg to order every camp in the headquarters to conduct strict searches as well. Those who had sent captives home ahead of the army should be given provisions in measured amounts and all escorted back to the submission stockade.
translations.idiomatic: I also ask that every headquarters camp be searched. Anyone who sent captives home early should receive rations and be marched back to the submission camp.

sentences.zh: 其六，乞置九隴行縣於招安寨中，以前南鄭令王丕攝縣令，設置曹局，撫理百姓，擇其子弟之壯者，給帖使自入山招其親戚；

translations.literal: Sixth, I beg to establish the provisional county of Jiulong within the submission stockade, with the former magistrate of Nanzheng, Wang Pi, acting as magistrate, setting up offices to govern the people, and selecting strong youths among them, giving them passes to go into the mountains themselves and bring in their kin;
translations.idiomatic: Sixth, set up Jiulong County inside the submission camp, with former Nanzheng magistrate Wang Pi as acting magistrate, establish offices, and give passes to strong local youths to bring in their kin from the hills;

sentences.zh: 彼知司徒嚴禁侵掠，前日為軍士所虜者，皆獲安堵，必歡呼踴躍，相帥下山，如子歸母，不日盡出。

translations.literal: when they know the Minister of Works strictly forbids plunder and that those seized by soldiers the other day have all been settled in peace, they will surely shout for joy and leap with eagerness, leading one another down the mountains like sons returning to a mother, and in no long time all will come out.
translations.idiomatic: Once they know you forbid plunder and that yesterday's captives are safe, they will come down shouting for joy, like sons to a mother, until none are left in the hills.

sentences.zh: 其七，彭州土地宜麻，百姓未入山時多漚藏者，宜令縣令曉諭，各歸田裡，出所漚麻鬻之，以為資糧，必漸復業。」

translations.literal: Seventh, Pengzhou's soil suits hemp. Before the people fled to the mountains many had soaked and stored it. The magistrate should instruct them to return to their fields, bring out the soaked hemp and sell it for provisions, and they will surely gradually resume their livelihoods."
translations.idiomatic: Seventh, Pengzhou soil suits hemp. Tell the magistrate to urge people back to their fields to sell stored hemp for food—they will slowly rebuild their lives."

sentences.zh: 建得之大喜，即行之，悉如所申。

translations.literal: Jian was greatly pleased on receiving this and immediately put it into practice, all exactly as requested.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was delighted and carried it out exactly as proposed.

sentences.zh: 明日，榜帖至，威令赫然，無敢犯者。

translations.literal: The next day the placards arrived; authority and orders were awe-inspiring, and none dared violate them.
translations.idiomatic: Next day the placards went up; discipline was fierce and none dared break it.

sentences.zh: 三日，山中民競出，赴招安寨如歸市，寨不能容，斥而廣之；

translations.literal: Within three days the mountain people rushed out and flocked to the submission stockade as to a market; the stockade could not hold them and was expanded by clearing more ground;
translations.idiomatic: Within three days the mountain people poured to the submission camp like a market crowd; the camp overflowed and was enlarged;

sentences.zh: 浸有市井，又出麻鬻之。

translations.literal: gradually a market appeared, and they brought out hemp to sell.
translations.idiomatic: shops appeared, and they sold their hemp.

sentences.zh: 民見村落無抄暴之患，稍稍辭縣令，復故業。

translations.literal: When the people saw that the villages were free of raiding and violence, they gradually took leave of the magistrate and returned to their former occupations.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing villages safe from raids, people gradually left the magistrate and went back to their old trades.

sentences.zh: 月餘，招安寨皆空。

translations.literal: After more than a month the submission stockades were all empty.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month the submission camps stood empty.

sentences.zh: 己巳，李茂貞克鳳州，感義節度使滿存奔興元。

translations.literal: On the day jisi, Li Maozhen captured Fengzhou. Man Cun, military governor of Ganyi, fled to Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, Li Maozhen took Fengzhou. Man Cun of Ganyi fled to Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 茂貞又取興、洋二州，皆表其子弟鎮之。

translations.literal: Maozhen also took the two prefectures of Xing and Yang, memorializing in each case that his sons and nephews be stationed there as governors.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen also seized Xing and Yang and had his kinsmen appointed to govern them.

sentences.zh: 八月，以楊行密為淮南節度使、同平章事，以田頵知宣州留後，安仁義為潤州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Yang Xingmi was appointed military governor of Huainan and Associate Chief Minister; Tian Jun was made acting prefect of Xuanzhou, and An Renyi prefect of Runzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Yang Xingmi became Huainan governor and Associate Chief Minister; Tian Jun held Xuanzhou, An Renyi Runzhou.

sentences.zh: 孫儒降兵多蔡人，行密選其尤勇健者五千人，厚其稟賜，以皁衣蒙甲，號「黑雲都」，每戰，使之先登陷陳，四鄰畏之。

translations.literal: Many of Sun Ru's surrendered troops were men of Cai. Xingmi chose five thousand of the boldest and sturdiest, enriched their pay and rations, clad them in black over their armor, and called them the "Black Cloud Corps." In every battle he sent them first to storm the line, and the neighboring circuits feared them.
translations.idiomatic: Many of Sun Ru's surrendered men were from Cai. Xingmi picked five thousand of the toughest, paid them well, dressed them in black over armor as the "Black Cloud Corps," and sent them first in every assault—neighbors feared them.

sentences.zh: 行密以用度不足，欲以茶鹽易民布帛，掌書記舒城高勖曰：「兵火之餘，十室九空，又漁利以困之，將復離叛。

translations.literal: Xingmi, finding revenues insufficient, wished to exchange tea and salt for the people's cloth and silk. His chief secretary Gao Xu of Shucheng said: "After the fires of war, nine houses in ten stand empty. To fish for profit and distress them further will drive them to rebel again.
translations.idiomatic: Short of funds, Xingmi wanted to trade tea and salt for cloth. Secretary Gao Xu said, "After the wars nine houses in ten are empty. Profiteering will drive them to rebel again.

sentences.zh: 不若悉我所有易鄰道所無，足以給軍；

translations.literal: Better to exchange all we have for what neighboring circuits lack—that will suffice to supply the army;
translations.idiomatic: Better trade what we have for what neighboring circuits lack—that will feed the army;

sentences.zh: 進賢守令勸課農桑，數年之間，倉庫自實。」

translations.literal: and have worthy magistrates urge farming and sericulture. Within a few years the granaries will fill of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: and have good officials promote farming. In a few years the granaries will fill themselves."

sentences.zh: 行密從之。

translations.literal: Xingmi followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi took his advice.

sentences.zh: 田頵聞之曰：「賢者之言，其利遠哉！」

translations.literal: Tian Jun heard of it and said: "The words of a worthy man—how far-reaching their benefit!"
translations.idiomatic: Tian Jun said, "A wise man's words bear fruit far in the future!"

sentences.zh: 行密馳射武伎，皆非所長，而寬簡有智略，善撫御將士，與同甘苦，推心待物，無所猜忌。

translations.literal: Xingmi was skilled neither at riding nor at archery nor at martial displays, but he was magnanimous and simple, possessed of strategy, good at winning over and commanding officers and men, sharing hardship and comfort with them, treating all with open heart and without suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi was no horseman, archer, or fighter, but he was generous and shrewd, treated his men as equals in hardship, and trusted people openly.

sentences.zh: 嘗早出，從者斷馬鞦，取其金，行密知而不問，它日，復早出如故，人服其度量。

translations.literal: Once when he went out early, a follower cut his saddle pommel and took the gold. Xingmi knew but did not inquire. Another day he went out early as before, and men admired his magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: Once a follower cut the gold from his saddle pommel; Xingmi knew but said nothing. When he went out early again as usual, men admired his forbearance.

sentences.zh: 淮南被兵六年，士民轉徙幾盡；

translations.literal: Huainan had suffered war for six years; soldiers and civilians had been uprooted almost to the last;
translations.idiomatic: Huainan had known war for six years; nearly all civilians had fled;

sentences.zh: 行密初至，賜與將吏，帛不過數尺，錢不過數百，而能以勤儉足用，非公宴，未嘗舉樂。

translations.literal: when Xingmi first arrived, gifts to officers and clerks were cloth of no more than a few feet and cash of no more than a few hundred, yet through diligence and frugality he made ends meet; except at public banquets he never had music performed.
translations.idiomatic: When Xingmi arrived, he gave officers only a few feet of cloth and a few hundred cash, yet lived frugally and never held music except at state banquets.

sentences.zh: 招撫流散，輕徭薄斂，未及數年，公私富庶，幾復承平之舊。

translations.literal: He brought in the scattered refugees, lightened corvée and taxes, and within a few years public and private stores were rich—almost the prosperity of peace restored.
translations.idiomatic: He resettled refugees, lightened taxes, and within years public and private wealth returned nearly to peacetime levels.

sentences.zh: 李克用北巡至天寧軍，聞李匡威、赫連鐸將兵八萬寇雲州，遣其將李君慶發兵於晉陽。

translations.literal: Li Keyong on his northern tour reached Tianning Army. Hearing that Li Kuangwei and Helian Duo were leading eighty thousand troops to invade Yunzhou, he sent his general Li Junqing to mobilize at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong on tour reached Tianning Army. Hearing Li Kuangwei and Helian Duo were marching eighty thousand against Yunzhou, he sent Li Junqing to mobilize at Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 克用潛入新城，伏兵於神堆，擒吐谷渾邏騎三百；

translations.literal: Keyong secretly entered Xincheng and ambushed at Shendui, capturing three hundred Tuyuhun patrol horsemen;
translations.idiomatic: Keyong slipped into Xincheng and ambushed at Shendui, taking three hundred Tuyuhun scouts;

sentences.zh: 匡威等大驚。

translations.literal: Kuangwei and the others were greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangwei and the rest were stunned.

sentences.zh: 丙申，君慶以大軍至，克用遷入雲州。

translations.literal: On the day bingshen, Junqing arrived with the main army and Keyong moved into Yunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, Junqing arrived with the main force and Keyong entered Yunzhou.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，出擊匡威等，大破之。

translations.literal: On the day dingyou he marched out to attack Kuangwei and the others and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou he struck Kuangwei and shattered them.

sentences.zh: 己亥，天威等燒營而遁；

translations.literal: On the day jihai, Tianwei and the others burned their camps and fled;
translations.idiomatic: On jihai they burned their camps and fled;

sentences.zh: 追至天成軍，斬獲不可勝計。

translations.literal: pursuit reached Tiancheng Army with kills and captures beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: pursuit to Tiancheng Army yielded kills and captures beyond count.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，李茂貞攻拔興元，楊復恭、楊守亮、楊守信、楊守貞、楊守忠、滿存奔閬州。

translations.literal: On the day xinchou, Li Maozhen attacked and took Xingyuan. Yang Fugong, Yang Shouliang, Yang Shouxin, Yang Shouzhen, Yang Shouzhong, and Man Cun fled to Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, Li Maozhen took Xingyuan. Yang Fugong, the Yang brothers, and Man Cun fled to Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 茂貞表其子繼密權知興元府事。

translations.literal: Maozhen memorialized that his son Jimi be appointed acting administrator of Xingyuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen had his son Jimi made acting administrator of Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 九月，加荊南節度使成汭同平章事。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Cheng Ru, military governor of Jingnan, was given the additional title of Associate Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Cheng Ru of Jingnan was made Associate Chief Minister.

sentences.zh: 時溥迫監軍奏稱將士留己，冬，十月，復以溥為侍中、感化節度。

translations.literal: Shi Pu compelled the supervising eunuch to memorialize that the troops wished him to remain. In winter, the tenth month, Pu was again appointed Palace Attendant and military governor of Ganhua.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Pu forced the supervising eunuch to say the troops wanted him to stay. In the tenth month of winter he was again made Palace Attendant and Ganhua governor.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠奏請追溥新命；

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong memorialized requesting revocation of Pu's new appointment;
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong asked that Pu's new appointment be revoked;

sentences.zh: 詔諭解之。

translations.literal: an edict was issued instructing reconciliation.
translations.idiomatic: the court ordered them reconciled.

sentences.zh: 初，邢、洺、磁州留後李存孝，與李存信俱為李克用假子，不相睦。

translations.literal: Earlier, Li Cunxiao, acting commissioner of Xing, Ming, and Ci prefectures, and Li Cunxin were both adopted sons of Li Keyong and were not on good terms.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunxiao of Xing, Ming, and Ci and Li Cunxin were both Li Keyong's adopted sons and were at odds.

sentences.zh: 存信有寵於克用，存孝在邢州，欲立大功以勝之，乃建議取鎮冀；

translations.literal: Cunxin enjoyed Keyong's favor. Cunxiao, at Xingzhou, wished to win great merit to surpass him and therefore proposed seizing Zhen and Ji;
translations.idiomatic: Cunxin was Keyong's favorite. Cunxiao at Xingzhou sought glory to outdo him and proposed taking Zhen and Ji;

sentences.zh: 存信從中沮之，不時聽許。

translations.literal: Cunxin obstructed him from within and permission was not granted in timely fashion.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxin blocked him and Keyong would not approve.

sentences.zh: 及王鎔圍堯山，存孝救之，不克。

translations.literal: When Wang Rong besieged Yaoshan, Cunxiao went to rescue him but failed.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Rong besieged Yaoshan, Cunxiao failed to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 克用以存信為蕃、馬步都指揮使，與存孝共擊之，二人互相猜忌，逗留不進；

translations.literal: Keyong appointed Cunxin commander of all foreign and Han horse and foot and sent him with Cunxiao to attack. The two were mutually suspicious and lingered without advancing;
translations.idiomatic: Keyong sent Cunxin to join Cunxiao in the attack; they distrusted each other and stalled;

sentences.zh: 克用更遣李嗣勳等擊破之。

translations.literal: Keyong again dispatched Li Sixun and others, who defeated Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong sent Li Sixun, who broke Rong's force.

sentences.zh: 存信還，譖存孝無心擊賊，疑與之有私約。

translations.literal: Cunxin returned and slandered Cunxiao, saying he had no heart to strike the enemy and was suspected of a private pact with him.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxin returned and accused Cunxiao of holding back and colluding with the enemy.

sentences.zh: 存孝聞之，自以有功於克用，而信任顧不及存信，憤怨，且懼及禍，乃潛結王鎔及朱全忠，上表以三州自歸於朝廷，乞賜旌節及會諸道兵討李克用；

translations.literal: Cunxiao heard this. He considered that he had rendered merit to Keyong yet trust and favor fell short of Cunxin; angry and resentful, and fearing disaster, he secretly allied with Wang Rong and Zhu Quanzhong and submitted a memorial offering the three prefectures to the court, begging for an imperial banner and staff and for allied troops of the circuits to punish Li Keyong;
translations.idiomatic: Cunxiao, angry that Cunxin outranked him in favor and fearing ruin, secretly allied with Wang Rong and Zhu Quanzhong and offered his three prefectures to the throne, asking for a commission and allied armies against Li Keyong;

sentences.zh: 詔以存孝為邢、洺、磁節度使，不許會兵。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Cunxiao military governor of Xing, Ming, and Ci but did not permit allied armies.
translations.idiomatic: The court made Cunxiao governor of Xing, Ming, and Ci but denied allied troops.

sentences.zh: 十一月，時溥濠州刺史張璲、泗州刺史張諫以州附於朱全忠。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Zhang Lin, prefect of Hao in Shi's domain, and Zhang Jian, prefect of Si, surrendered their prefectures to Zhu Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Zhang Lin of Hao and Zhang Jian of Si surrendered to Zhu Quanzhong.

sentences.zh: 乙未，朱全忠遣其子友裕將兵十萬攻濮州，拔之，執其刺史邵倫，遂令友裕移兵擊時溥。

translations.literal: On the day yiwei, Zhu Quanzhong sent his son Youyu with a hundred thousand troops to attack Puzhou, took it, seized its prefect Shao Lun, and then ordered Youyu to shift his army against Shi Pu.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, Zhu Quanzhong sent Youyu with a hundred thousand men against Puzhou, took it, seized Prefect Shao Lun, and turned Youyu on Shi Pu.

sentences.zh: 孫儒將王壇陷婺州，刺史蔣環奔趙州。

translations.literal: Wang Tan, a general of Sun Ru, seized Wuzhou; its prefect Jiang Huan fled to Zhaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ru's general Wang Tan took Wuzhou; Prefect Jiang Huan fled to Zhaozhou.

sentences.zh: 廬州刺史蔡儔發楊行密祖父墓，與舒州刺史倪章連兵，遣使送印於朱全忠以求救。

translations.literal: Cai Chou, prefect of Luzhou, opened the tomb of Yang Xingmi's grandfather. Together with Ni Zhang, prefect of Shuzhou, he joined forces and sent envoys bearing his seal to Zhu Quanzhong to beg rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Chou of Luzhou desecrated Yang Xingmi's grandfather's tomb. With Ni Zhang of Shuzhou he sent his seal to Zhu Quanzhong begging for aid.

sentences.zh: 全忠惡其反覆，納其印，不救，且牒報行密；

translations.literal: Quanzhong despised his fickleness, accepted the seal but did not rescue him, and also sent a dispatch informing Xingmi;
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong despised his treachery, took the seal but sent no aid, and notified Xingmi;

sentences.zh: 行密謝之。

translations.literal: Xingmi thanked him.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi thanked him.

sentences.zh: 行密遣行營都指揮使李神福將兵討儔。

translations.literal: Xingmi dispatched his campaign commander Li Shenfu with troops to punish Chou.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi sent Li Shenfu to punish Chou.

sentences.zh: 《宣明歷》浸差，太子少詹事邊岡造新歷成，十二月，上之。

translations.literal: The Xuaming Calendar had gradually drifted. Bian Gang, Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent, completed a new calendar and presented it in the twelfth month.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuaming Calendar had drifted. Bian Gang finished a new calendar and presented it in the twelfth month.

sentences.zh: 命曰《景福崇玄歷》。

translations.literal: It was named the Jingfu Chongxuan Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: It was named the Jingfu Chongxuan Calendar.

sentences.zh: 壬午，王建遣其將華洪擊楊守亮於閬州，破之。

translations.literal: On the day renwu, Wang Jian sent his general Hua Hong to attack Yang Shouliang at Langzhou and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, Wang Jian sent Hua Hong against Yang Shouliang at Langzhou and broke him.

sentences.zh: 建遣節度押牙延陵鄭頊使於朱全忠；

translations.literal: Jian sent Zheng Xu of Yanling, adjutant of the circuit staff, as envoy to Zhu Quanzhong;
translations.idiomatic: Jian sent staff adjutant Zheng Xu of Yanling to Zhu Quanzhong;

sentences.zh: 全忠問劍閣，頊極言其險。

translations.literal: Quanzhong asked about Jian'ge Pass; Xu spoke at length of its peril.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong asked about Jian'ge Pass; Xu described its dangers at length.

sentences.zh: 全忠不信，頊曰：「苟不以聞，恐誤公軍機。」

translations.literal: Quanzhong did not believe him. Xu said: "If I do not speak of it, I fear I may mislead Your Lordship's military plans."
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong did not believe him. Xu said, "If I keep silent, I may mislead your campaign."

sentences.zh: 全忠大笑。

translations.literal: Quanzhong laughed loudly.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong laughed aloud.

sentences.zh: 是歲，明州刺史鐘文季卒，其將黃晟自稱刺史。

translations.literal: That year, Zhong Wenji, prefect of Mingzhou, died; his general Huang Sheng declared himself prefect.
translations.idiomatic: That year Mingzhou prefect Zhong Wenji died; his general Huang Sheng seized the post.

sentences.zh: 昭宗聖穆景文孝皇帝上之中景福二年（

translations.literal: Second year of the Jingfu era of Emperor Zhaozong, the Sagacious, Reverent, Cultivated, and Filial, upper fascicle, middle section (
translations.idiomatic: Second year of the Jingfu era of Emperor Zhaozong (upper fascicle, middle section) (

sentences.zh: 癸丑，公元八九三年）

translations.literal: guichou, corresponding to the year 893 CE)
translations.idiomatic: the year guichou, equivalent to 893 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，時溥遣兵攻宿州，刺史郭言戰死。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Shi Pu dispatched troops to attack Suzhou; its prefect Guo Yan died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Shi Pu attacked Suzhou; Prefect Guo Yan was killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 東川留後顧彥暉既與王建有隙，李茂貞欲撫之使從己，秦恢復更賜彥暉節；

translations.literal: Gu Yanhui, acting commissioner of Dongchuan, was already at odds with Wang Jian. Li Maozhen wished to win him to his side. Qin Hui again invested Yanhui with a banner and staff;
translations.idiomatic: Gu Yanhui of Dongchuan was at odds with Wang Jian. Li Maozhen sought to win him. Qin Hui again granted Yanhui a commission;

sentences.zh: 詔以彥暉為東川節度使，茂貞又奏遣知興元府事李繼密救梓州，未幾，建遣兵敗東川、鳳翔之兵於利州，彥暉求和，請與茂貞絕。

translations.literal: an edict appointed Yanhui military governor of Dongchuan. Maozhen also memorialized sending Jimi, acting administrator of Xingyuan, to rescue Zizhou. Before long, Jian sent troops and defeated the Dongchuan and Fengxiang armies at Lizhou. Yanhui sued for peace and asked to break with Maozhen.
translations.idiomatic: Yanhui was made Dongchuan governor. Maozhen sent Jimi to relieve Zizhou. Soon Jian defeated Dongchuan and Fengxiang at Lizhou; Yanhui sued for peace and broke with Maozhen.

sentences.zh: 乃許之。

translations.literal: Permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔節度使李茂貞自請鎮興元，詔以茂貞為山南西道兼武定節度使，以中書侍郎、同平章事徐彥若同平章事，充鳳翔節度使，又割果、閬二州隸武定軍。

translations.literal: Li Maozhen, military governor of Fengxiang, requested to be stationed at Xingyuan himself. An edict appointed Maozhen military governor of Shannan West and Wuding concurrently, made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Chief Minister Xu Yanruo Associate Chief Minister and military governor of Fengxiang, and detached the two prefectures of Guo and Lang to Wuding Army.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen asked to hold Xingyuan. The court made him governor of Shannan West and Wuding, sent Xu Yanruo to Fengxiang, and attached Guo and Lang to Wuding.

sentences.zh: 茂貞欲兼得鳳翔，不奉詔。

translations.literal: Maozhen wished to hold Fengxiang as well and did not obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen wanted Fengxiang too and refused the edict.

sentences.zh: 二月，甲戌，加西川節度使王建同平章事。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day jiaxu, Wang Jian, military governor of Xichuan, was given the additional title of Associate Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on jiaxu, Wang Jian of Xichuan was made Associate Chief Minister.

sentences.zh: 李克用引兵圍邢州，王鎔遣牙將王藏海致書解之，克用怒，斬藏海，進兵擊鎔，敗鎮兵於平山，辛巳，攻天長鎮，旬日不下。

translations.literal: Li Keyong besieged Xingzhou. Wang Rong sent Wang Zanghai to negotiate; Keyong beheaded him and beat Rong's army at Pingshan. On xinsi he attacked Tianchang Fort for ten days without success.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong besieged Xingzhou. Wang Rong sent Wang Zanghai to negotiate; Keyong beheaded him and beat Rong's army at Pingshan. On xinsi he attacked Tianchang Fort for ten days without success.

sentences.zh: 鎔出兵三萬救之，克用逆戰於叱日嶺下，大破之，斬首萬餘級，餘眾潰去。

translations.literal: Rong marched out thirty thousand to relieve it. Keyong met them below Chiri Ridge and routed them utterly, beheading more than ten thousand; the rest fled in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Rong sent thirty thousand to relieve it. Keyong met them at Chiri Ridge, killed more than ten thousand, and routed the rest.

sentences.zh: 河東軍無食。

translations.literal: The Hedong army had no food.
translations.idiomatic: The Hedong army starved.

sentences.zh: 脯其屍而啖之。

translations.literal: They dried human flesh as jerky and ate it.
translations.idiomatic: They ate the flesh of the dead.

sentences.zh: 時溥求救於朱瑾，朱全忠遣其將霍存將騎兵三千軍曹州以備之。

translations.literal: Shi Pu begged Zhu Jin for rescue. Zhu Quanzhong sent his general Huo Cun with three thousand cavalry to garrison Caozhou in readiness.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Pu begged Zhu Jin for aid. Zhu Quanzhong posted Huo Cun with three thousand horse at Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 瑾將兵二萬救徐州，存引兵赴之，與朱友裕合擊徐、兗兵於石佛山下，大破之，瑾遁歸兗州。

translations.literal: Jin led twenty thousand troops to rescue Xuzhou. Cun marched to meet them and, joining Zhu Youyu, struck the Xu and Yan armies below Mount Shifo and routed them; Jin fled back to Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jin marched twenty thousand to save Xuzhou. Cun joined Youyu and shattered the Xu and Yan forces at Mount Shifo; Jin fled to Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，徐兵復出，存戰死。

translations.literal: On the day xinmao the Xu troops came out again; Cun died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao the Xu troops sallied again and Cun was killed.

sentences.zh: 李克用進下井陘，李存孝將兵救王鎔，遂入鎮州，與鎔計事，鎔又乞師於朱全忠，全忠方與時溥相攻，不能救，但遺克用書，言「鄴下有十萬精兵，抑而未進。」

translations.literal: Li Keyong advanced down Jingxing Pass. Li Cunxiao led troops to rescue Wang Rong, entered Zhenzhou, and consulted with Rong. Rong again begged Zhu Quanzhong for troops. Quanzhong was then attacking Shi Pu and could not rescue him, but sent Keyong a letter saying: "Below Ye there are a hundred thousand elite troops, held back and not yet advanced."
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong advanced through Jingxing Pass. Li Cunxiao entered Zhenzhou to aid Wang Rong. Rong begged Zhu Quanzhong, who was fighting Shi Pu and could not help, but wrote Keyong that "a hundred thousand elite troops below Ye are held back."

sentences.zh: 克用復書：「倘實屯軍鄴下，顒望降臨；

translations.literal: Keyong replied: "If troops are truly encamped below Ye, I look forward to their descent upon me;
translations.idiomatic: Keyong replied, "If they truly camp below Ye, I await them;

sentences.zh: 必欲真決雌雄，願角逐於常山之尾。」

translations.literal: if you truly wish to settle supremacy, I wish to contend at the tail of Mount Chang."
translations.idiomatic: if you wish a true contest, meet me at the foot of Mount Chang."

sentences.zh: 甲午，李匡威引兵救鎔，敗河東兵於元氏，克用引還邢州。

translations.literal: On the day jiawu, Li Kuangwei led troops to rescue Rong and defeated the Hedong army at Yuanshi. Keyong withdrew to Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, Li Kuangwei relieved Rong and beat Hedong at Yuanshi. Keyong fell back to Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 鎔犒匡威於蒿城，輦金帛二十萬以酬之。

translations.literal: Rong feasted Kuangwei at Haocheng and sent twenty thousand in gold and silk as reward.
translations.idiomatic: Rong feasted Kuangwei at Haocheng and gave him two hundred thousand in gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 朱友裕圍彭城，時溥數出兵，友裕閉壁不戰。

translations.literal: Zhu Youyu besieged Pengcheng. Shi Pu sallied repeatedly; Youyu shut the walls and would not fight.
translations.idiomatic: Youyu besieged Pengcheng. Shi Pu sallied often; Youyu held the walls and would not fight.

sentences.zh: 朱瑾宵遁，友裕不追，都虞候朱友恭以書譖友裕於全忠。

translations.literal: Zhu Jin fled by night. Youyu did not pursue. The chief overseeing officer Zhu Yougong slandered Youyu to Quanzhong in a letter.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Jin fled by night. Youyu did not pursue. Zhu Yougong wrote Quanzhong accusing Youyu.

sentences.zh: 全忠怒，驛書下都指揮使龐師古，使代之將，且按其事。

translations.literal: Quanzhong was angry and sent a dispatch by post to the supreme commander Pang Shigu ordering him to replace Youyu in command and investigate the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong in anger ordered Pang Shigu to replace Youyu and investigate.

sentences.zh: 書誤達於友裕，友裕大懼，以二千騎逃入山中，潛詣碭山，匿於伯父全昱之所。

translations.literal: The letter by mistake reached Youyu. Youyu was greatly afraid and fled into the mountains with two thousand horsemen, secretly going to Dangshan and hiding at the home of his uncle Quanyu.
translations.idiomatic: The letter reached Youyu by mistake. Terrified, he fled to the hills with two thousand horse and hid with his uncle Quanyu at Dangshan.

sentences.zh: 全忠夫人張氏聞之，使友裕單騎詣汴州見全忠，泣涕拜伏於庭；

translations.literal: Quanzhong's wife, Lady Zhang, heard of it and had Youyu come alone on horseback to Bianzhou to see Quanzhong, weeping and prostrating himself in the courtyard;
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhang had Youyu ride alone to Bianzhou, where he wept and prostrated himself before Quanzhong;

sentences.zh: 全忠命左右捽抑，將斬之，夫人趨就抱之，泣曰「汝捨兵眾，束身歸罪，無異志明矣。」

translations.literal: Quanzhong ordered his attendants to seize and hold him down to behead him. The lady rushed forward and embraced him, weeping: "You abandoned your troops and came alone to accept guilt—no different from Zhiming."
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong ordered him seized for execution. Lady Zhang embraced him, weeping, "You left your army to accept blame—like Zhiming himself."

sentences.zh: 全忠悟而捨之，使權知許州。

translations.literal: Quanzhong understood and released him, appointing him acting administrator of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong relented and made him acting administrator of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 友恭，壽春人李彥威也，幼為全忠家僮，全忠養以為子。

translations.literal: Yougong was Li Yanwei of Shouchun, taken as a household slave in Quanzhong's home in youth; Quanzhong raised him as a son.
translations.idiomatic: Yougong was Li Yanwei of Shouchun, a household slave Quanzhong raised as a son.

sentences.zh: 張夫人，碭山人，多智略，全忠敬憚之，雖軍府事，時與之謀議；

translations.literal: Lady Zhang was from Dangshan, possessed of much strategy; Quanzhong respected and feared her, and even in military headquarters affairs he often deliberated with her;
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhang of Dangshan was shrewd; Quanzhong respected and feared her and often consulted her on military affairs;

sentences.zh: 或將兵出，中途，夫人以為不可，遣一介召之，全忠立為之返。

translations.literal: when he was marching out with troops, if midway the lady thought it inadvisable she would send a single messenger to summon him, and Quanzhong would immediately turn back.
translations.idiomatic: if she thought a campaign ill-advised she would send a messenger mid-march and Quanzhong would turn back at once.

sentences.zh: 龐師古攻佛山寨，撥之，自是徐兵不敢出。

translations.literal: Pang Shigu attacked the Foshan stockade and took it; from then on the Xu troops dared not sally.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Shigu stormed the Foshan stockade; thereafter Xu's men dared not come out.

sentences.zh: 李匡威之救王鎔也，將發幽州，家人會別，弟匡籌之妻美，匡威醉而淫之。

translations.literal: When Li Kuangwei was about to set out from Youzhou to rescue Wang Rong, the family gathered to bid farewell. His younger brother Kuangchou's wife was beautiful; Kuangwei, drunk, violated her.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Kuangwei was leaving Youzhou to save Wang Rong, the family gathered to farewell. Drunk, he violated his brother Kuangchou's beautiful wife.

sentences.zh: 二月，匡威自鎮州還，至博野，匡籌據軍府自稱留後，以符追行營兵。

translations.literal: In the second month, Kuangwei returned from Zhenzhou. Reaching Boye, Kuangchou seized the headquarters and declared himself acting commissioner, using tally-sticks to recall the campaign troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Kuangwei returned from Zhenzhou. At Boye, Kuangchou seized headquarters, declared himself acting commissioner, and recalled the army.

sentences.zh: 匡威眾潰歸，但與親近留深州，進退無所之，遣判官李抱真入奏，請歸京師。

translations.literal: Kuangwei's troops scattered and returned; he remained only with close followers at Shenzhou, with nowhere to go forward or back, and sent his aide Li Baozhen to memorialize the throne requesting return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangwei's army dissolved; he lingered at Shenzhou with a few followers and sent Li Baozhen to ask leave to return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 京師屢更大亂，聞匡威來，坊市大恐，曰：「金頭王來圖社稷。」

translations.literal: The capital had suffered great disorder repeatedly. Hearing Kuangwei was coming, the wards and markets were greatly afraid, saying: "The Gold-Headed King comes to seize the realm."
translations.idiomatic: The capital had known repeated chaos. Hearing Kuangwei was coming, the city panicked, saying, "The Gold-Headed King comes for the throne."

sentences.zh: 士民或竄匿山谷。

translations.literal: Civilians and commoners fled and hid in the mountains and valleys.
translations.idiomatic: People hid in the hills.

sentences.zh: 王鎔德其以己故致失地，迎歸鎮州，為築第，父事之。

translations.literal: Wang Rong was grateful that Kuangwei had lost his territory on his account; he welcomed him back to Zhenzhou, built him a mansion, and treated him as a father.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong, grateful that Kuangwei had lost his domain for his sake, welcomed him to Zhenzhou, built him a mansion, and treated him like a father.

sentences.zh: 以渝州刺史柳玭為瀘州刺史，柳氏自化綽以來，世以孝悌禮法為士大夫所宗。

translations.literal: Liu Pin, prefect of Yu, was appointed prefect of Lu. Since Liuhua Chuo's time the Liu clan had been honored by scholar-officials for filial piety, brotherly duty, and ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Pin of Yu was made prefect of Lu. Since Liuhua Chuo the Liu clan had been famed among scholars for filial piety and ritual.

sentences.zh: 玼御史大夫，上欲以為相。

translations.literal: Cī was Vice Censor-in-Chief; the Emperor wished to appoint him Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Cī served as Vice Censor-in-Chief, and the Emperor meant to make him Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 宦官惡之，故久謫於外。

translations.literal: The eunuchs hated him, and so he was long relegated to posts beyond the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs hated him, and for long he was kept in exile far from court.

sentences.zh: 玼戒其子弟曰：「凡門地高，可畏不可恃也。

translations.literal: Cī admonished his sons and younger kin, saying: "When one's family station is lofty, it is to be feared, not to be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: Cī warned his sons and younger relatives: "A house of high standing inspires awe, yet offers no sure footing.

sentences.zh: 立身行己，一事有失，是得罪重於他人，死無以見先人於地下，此其所以可畏也。

translations.literal: In how one stands in the world and conducts oneself, a single lapse means the offense weighs heavier than others'; in death one has no face to meet one's forebears beneath the earth—this is why it is to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: In conduct and self-discipline, one misstep counts for more than it would for others; dead, you cannot face your ancestors in the dark below—that is what makes a great house fearsome.

sentences.zh: 門高則驕心易生，族盛則為人所嫉；

translations.literal: When the gate is high, an arrogant heart easily arises; when the clan is great, others grow jealous;
translations.idiomatic: A lofty gate breeds pride; a flourishing clan draws envy;

sentences.zh: 懿行實才，人未之信，小有玼，眾皆指之。

translations.literal: Though one's fine conduct and real talent go unbelieved, the slightest blemish—all point at it.
translations.idiomatic: Even with sterling virtue and genuine talent, men withhold their trust; let the smallest flaw appear, and every finger turns on you.

sentences.zh: 此其所以不可恃也。

translations.literal: This is why it cannot be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: That is why high birth is no thing to lean on.

sentences.zh: 故膏梁子弟，學宜加勤，行宜加勵，僅得比他人耳！」

translations.literal: Therefore the sons of rich families should study all the more diligently and conduct themselves all the more strictly—only then may they barely compare with others!"
translations.idiomatic: So the pampered sons of great houses must study harder and walk more carefully—and even then they may only hope to stand equal to other men!"

sentences.zh: 王建屢請殺陳敬瑄、田令孜、朝廷不許。

translations.literal: Wang Jian repeatedly requested that Chen Jingxuan and Tian Lingzi be put to death; the court would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian repeatedly petitioned for the execution of Chen Jingxuan and Tian Lingzi, but the court refused.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，乙亥，建使人告敬瑄謀作亂，殺之新津。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the day yihai, Jian sent men to report that Jingxuan was plotting rebellion, and had him killed at Xinjin.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on yihai, Wang Jian had agents accuse Chen Jingxuan of plotting rebellion and had him slain at Xinjin.

sentences.zh: 又告令孜通鳳翔書，下獄死。

translations.literal: He further reported that Lingzi had exchanged letters with Fengxiang; Lingzi was cast into prison and died there.
translations.idiomatic: He also accused Tian Lingzi of corresponding with Fengxiang; Tian was thrown into prison and died there.

sentences.zh: 建使節度判官馮涓草表奏之曰：「開匣出虎，孔宣父不責他人；

translations.literal: Jian had his circuit judge Feng Juan draft a memorial stating: "When one opens the casket and releases the tiger, Confucius did not blame others;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian had his circuit judge Feng Juan draft a memorial saying: "To open the box and let loose the tiger—the Master did not fault another for that;

sentences.zh: 當路斬蛇，孫叔敖蓋非利己。

translations.literal: When one cuts down the serpent blocking the road, Sun Shuao surely did not act for his own profit.
translations.idiomatic: To strike down the serpent in the path—Sun Shuao hardly did it for selfish gain.

sentences.zh: 專殺不行於閫外，先機恐失於彀中。」

translations.literal: Summary execution may not be exercised outside the commander's tent; yet to lose the first chance is to fear missing the prey within the snare."
translations.idiomatic: The law forbids unauthorized killing beyond the camp gate, yet to wait on ceremony is to let the decisive moment slip through the net."

sentences.zh: 涓，宿之孫也。

translations.literal: Feng Juan was the grandson of Feng Su.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Juan was a grandson of Feng Su.

sentences.zh: 汴軍攻徐州，累月不克。

translations.literal: The Bian army besieged Xuzhou for months without taking it.
translations.idiomatic: The Bian armies assaulted Xuzhou month after month and could not break it.

sentences.zh: 通事官張濤以書白朱全忠云：「進軍時日非良，故無功。」

translations.literal: The liaison officer Zhang Tao wrote to Zhu Quanzhong, saying: "The day chosen for the advance was ill-omened, hence no success."
translations.idiomatic: The communications officer Zhang Tao wrote Zhu Quanzhong: "The day of advance was ill-chosen—that is why we have failed."

sentences.zh: 全忠以為然，敬翔曰：「今攻城累月，所費甚多，徐人已困，旦夕且下，使將士聞此言，則懈於攻取矣。」

translations.literal: Quanzhong thought this correct, but Jing Xiang said: "We have besieged the city for months at great cost; the men of Xu are already exhausted and will fall any day. If the troops hear this, they will slacken in the assault."
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong agreed, but Jing Xiang said: "We have spent months and a fortune on this siege; the Xu defenders are spent and will fall soon. Let the men hear this, and their will to press the attack will fail."

sentences.zh: 全忠乃焚其書。

translations.literal: Quanzhong thereupon burned the letter.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong burned the letter.

sentences.zh: 癸未，全忠自將如徐州；

translations.literal: On the day guiwei, Quanzhong personally led his forces toward Xuzhou;
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei, Quanzhong himself marched on Xuzhou;

sentences.zh: 戊子，龐師古撥彭城，時溥舉族登燕子樓自焚死。

translations.literal: On the day wuzi, Pang Shigu stormed Pengcheng; Shi Pu brought his whole clan up the Swallow Tower and burned themselves to death.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, Pang Shigu took Pengcheng; Shi Pu led his entire household up the Swallow Tower and perished in the flames.

sentences.zh: 己丑，全忠入彭城，以宋州刺史張廷范知感化留後，奏乞朝廷除文臣為節度使。

translations.literal: On the day jichou, Quanzhong entered Pengcheng, appointed Songzhou prefect Zhang Tingfan acting regent of Ganhua, and memorialized asking the court to appoint a civil official as military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Quanzhong entered Pengcheng, set Songzhou prefect Zhang Tingfan to govern Ganhua as acting regent, and petitioned the throne to name a civil official as military governor.

sentences.zh: 李匡威在鎮州，為王鎔完城塹，繕甲兵，訓士卒，視之如子，匡威以鎔年少，且樂真定土風，潛謀奪之。

translations.literal: Li Kuangwei was at Zhenzhou; he repaired Wang Rong's walls and moats, readied arms and armor, trained the soldiers, and treated them like sons. Kuangwei, thinking Rong young and himself enamored of the ways of Zhending, secretly plotted to seize the province.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kuangwei was at Zhenzhou, where he rebuilt Wang Rong's walls and ditches, repaired arms and armor, drilled the troops, and treated them as his own sons. Seeing Rong still young, and himself charmed by the ways of Zhending, he secretly plotted to take the command from him.

sentences.zh: 李抱真自京師還，為之畫策，陰以恩施悅其將士。

translations.literal: Li Baozhen returned from the capital and devised plans for him, secretly winning over the officers and soldiers with favors.
translations.idiomatic: Li Baozhen, back from the capital, laid plans for him and quietly bought the loyalty of officers and men with kindness.

sentences.zh: 王氏在鎮久，鎮人愛之，不徇匡威。

translations.literal: The Wang house had long ruled the command; the people loved them and would not follow Kuangwei.
translations.idiomatic: The Wangs had held the command long; the people loved them and would not heed Kuangwei.

sentences.zh: 匡威忌日，鎔就第吊之。

translations.literal: On the anniversary of Kuangwei's father's death, Rong went to his residence to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: On the anniversary of Kuangwei's father's death, Rong went in person to his house to mourn.

sentences.zh: 匡威素服衷甲，伏兵劫之，鎔趨抱匡威曰：「鎔為晉人所困，幾亡矣，賴公以有今日；

translations.literal: Kuangwei wore mourning garb over hidden armor and set ambushers to seize him. Rong rushed forward and embraced Kuangwei, saying: "Rong was hard pressed by the men of Jin and nearly destroyed; I owe my survival today to you;
translations.idiomatic: Kuangwei wore plain mourning dress over mail and set men in ambush. Rong ran to him and clasped him, saying: "I was beset by the Jin armies and nearly lost everything; it was you who gave me this day;

sentences.zh: 公欲得四州，此固鎔之願也，不若與公共歸府，以位讓公，則將土莫之拒矣。」

translations.literal: If you wish the four prefectures, that is indeed Rong's wish as well. Better to return with me to headquarters and yield the post to you—then none of the officers and soldiers will refuse."
translations.idiomatic: If you want the four prefectures, that has long been my wish. Come back with me to headquarters and I will yield the command—then none of the officers and men will stand against you."

sentences.zh: 匡威不以為然，與鎔駢馬，陳兵入府，會大風雷雨，屋瓦皆振。
