translations.literal: Kuangwei would not agree; he rode side by side with Rong at the head of armed men into headquarters. A great wind and thunderstorm arose, and every roof tile shook.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangwei would not have it. He rode beside Rong at the head of armed men into headquarters. A violent storm broke; roof tiles shook in the wind.

sentences.zh: 匡威入東偏門，鎮之親軍閉之，有屠者墨君和自缺垣躍出，拳毆匡威甲士，挾鎔於馬上，負之登屋。

translations.literal: Kuangwei entered the eastern side gate; the command's personal guard shut it behind him. A butcher named Mo Junhe leapt from a broken wall, fisted Kuangwei's armored men, seized Rong on horseback, and carried him up onto a roof.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangwei entered by the eastern side gate; the garrison's personal guard closed it behind him. A butcher named Mo Junhe vaulted through a breach in the wall, beat Kuangwei's armored men with his fists, snatched Rong from the saddle, and bore him up onto a rooftop.

sentences.zh: 鎮人既得鎔，攻匡威，殺之，並其族黨。

translations.literal: Once the people of the command had Rong back, they turned on Kuangwei, killed him, and wiped out his kin and partisans.
translations.idiomatic: When the men of the command had Rong safe again, they fell on Kuangwei, killed him, and destroyed his clan and followers.

sentences.zh: 鎔時年十七，體疏瘦，為君和所挾，頸痛頭偏者累日。

translations.literal: Rong was then seventeen, slight and thin; seized by Junhe, his neck ached and his head hung crooked for days.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was only seventeen, slight of build; after Junhe's rescue his neck ached and his head hung askew for days.

sentences.zh: 李匡籌奏鎔殺其兄，請舉兵復冤；

translations.literal: Li Kuangchou memorialized that Rong had killed his elder brother and requested to raise troops to avenge the wrong;
translations.idiomatic: Li Kuangchou reported that Rong had killed his elder brother and asked leave to raise an army and right the wrong;

sentences.zh: 詔不許。

translations.literal: An edict forbade it.
translations.idiomatic: The throne refused.

sentences.zh: 幽州將劉仁恭將兵戍蔚州，過期未代，士卒思歸。

translations.literal: Youzhou general Liu Rengong led troops garrisoning Weizhou; their term expired yet no relief came, and the soldiers longed to return home.
translations.idiomatic: The Youzhou general Liu Rengong held Weizhou with a garrison whose tour had expired without relief, and the men yearned for home.

sentences.zh: 會李匡籌立，戍卒奉仁恭為帥，還攻幽州，至居庸關，為府兵所敗。

translations.literal: When Li Kuangchou came to power, the garrison troops made Rengong their commander, marched back to attack Youzhou, reached Juyong Pass, and were defeated by the headquarters troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Kuangchou took power, the garrison troops raised Rengong as their leader, turned back to strike Youzhou, reached Juyong Pass, and were beaten by the headquarters army.

sentences.zh: 仁恭奔河東，李克用厚待之。

translations.literal: Rengong fled to Hedong, where Li Keyong treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: Rengong fled to Hedong, where Li Keyong received him with great favor.

sentences.zh: 李神福圍廬州；

translations.literal: Li Shenfu besieged Luzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Li Shenfu besieged Luzhou;

sentences.zh: 甲午，楊行密自將詣廬州，田頵自宣州引兵會之。

translations.literal: On the day jiawu, Yang Xingmi personally led his forces to Luzhou; Tian Jun brought troops from Xuanzhou to join him.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, Yang Xingmi marched on Luzhou in person, and Tian Jun led troops from Xuanzhou to meet him.

sentences.zh: 初，蔡人張顥以驍勇事秦宗權，後從孫儒，儒敗，歸行密，行密厚待之，使將兵戍廬州。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Cai native Zhang Hao, known for fierce valor, had served Qin Zongquan, then followed Sun Ru; when Ru was defeated he joined Xingmi, who treated him generously and put him in command of the Luzhou garrison.
translations.idiomatic: At first the Cai man Zhang Hao, a fierce fighter, had served Qin Zongquan, then Sun Ru; when Ru fell, he came to Yang Xingmi, who treated him well and set him to garrison Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 蔡儔叛，顥更為之用。

translations.literal: When Cai Chou rebelled, Hao again served him.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai Chou rebelled, Hao went over to him.

sentences.zh: 及圍急，顥逾城來降，行密以隸銀槍都使袁稹。

translations.literal: When the siege grew desperate, Hao climbed over the wall to surrender; Xingmi assigned him to Silver Spear Commander Yuan Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: When the siege tightened, Hao climbed the wall to surrender; Yang Xingmi placed him under Silver Spear Commander Yuan Zhen.

sentences.zh: 稹以顥反覆，白行密，請殺之，行密恐稹不能容，置之親軍。

translations.literal: Zhen, finding Hao fickle, reported to Xingmi and asked that he be killed; Xingmi feared Zhen could not tolerate him and placed Hao in his personal guard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen, deeming Hao untrustworthy, asked Xingmi to kill him; fearing Zhen could not abide him, Xingmi kept Hao in his personal guard instead.

sentences.zh: 稹，陳州人也。

translations.literal: Zhen was a native of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was from Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 王彥復、王審知攻福州，久不下。

translations.literal: Wang Yanfu and Wang Shenzhi besieged Fuzhou for long without taking it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanfu and Wang Shenzhi assaulted Fuzhou for months without success.

sentences.zh: 范暉求救於威勝節度使董昌，昌與陳巖婚姻，發溫、台、婺州兵五千救之。

translations.literal: Fan Hui sought rescue from Weisheng military governor Dong Chang; Chang was allied by marriage with Chen Yan and sent five thousand troops from Wen, Tai, and Wuzhou to relieve the city.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Hui appealed to Weisheng military governor Dong Chang; bound to Chen Yan by marriage, Chang sent five thousand men from Wen, Tai, and Wuzhou to his aid.

sentences.zh: 彥復、審知以城堅，援兵且至，士卒死傷多，白王潮，欲罷兵更圖後舉，潮不許。

translations.literal: Yanfu and Shenzhi, finding the walls strong, relief near at hand, and their soldiers suffering heavy casualties, reported to Wang Chao and wished to withdraw and plan another attempt; Chao would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Yanfu and Shenzhi reported to Wang Chao that the walls were strong, relief was coming, and their men were dying in numbers; they wished to break off and try again later. Chao refused.

sentences.zh: 請潮自臨行營，潮報曰：「兵盡添兵，將盡添將，兵將俱盡，吾當自來。」

translations.literal: They asked Chao to come personally to the camp; Chao replied: "When the soldiers are exhausted, send more soldiers; when the generals are exhausted, send more generals; when soldiers and generals alike are exhausted, then I shall come myself."
translations.idiomatic: They asked Chao to come to the front in person. He answered: "When your soldiers are spent, send more soldiers; when your generals are spent, send more generals; when both are spent, then I shall come myself."

sentences.zh: 彥復、審知懼，親犯矢石急攻之。

translations.literal: Yanfu and Shenzhi, afraid, personally braved arrows and stones and pressed the assault.
translations.idiomatic: Afraid, Yanfu and Shenzhi threw themselves into the hail of arrows and stone and pressed the attack.

sentences.zh: 五月，城中食盡，暉知不能守，夜，以印授監軍，棄城走，援兵亦還。

translations.literal: In the fifth month food in the city was exhausted; Hui knew he could not hold out. By night he handed his seal to the army supervisor, abandoned the city and fled, and the relief force withdrew as well.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the city ran out of food. Hui saw he could not hold; that night he gave his seal to the army supervisor, abandoned the city and fled, and the relief army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 庚子，彥復等入城。

translations.literal: On the day gengzi, Yanfu and the others entered the city.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, Yanfu and his men entered the city.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，暉亡抵沿海都，為將士所殺。

translations.literal: On the day xinchou, the fugitive Hui reached Yanhai Command and was killed by officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, the fleeing Hui reached Yanhai Command and was killed by his own troops.

sentences.zh: 潮入福州，自稱留後，素服葬陳巖，以女妻其子延晦，厚撫其家。

translations.literal: Chao entered Fuzhou, styled himself acting regent, wore plain mourning to bury Chen Yan, gave his daughter in marriage to Yan's son Yanhui, and treated the family generously.
translations.idiomatic: Chao entered Fuzhou, took the title of acting regent, buried Chen Yan in plain mourning dress, gave his daughter to Yan's son Yanhui in marriage, and treated the household with great kindness.

sentences.zh: 汀、建二州降，嶺海間群盜二十餘輩皆降潰。

translations.literal: Ting and Jian prefectures surrendered; more than twenty bands of pirates between the mountains and the sea submitted or scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Ting and Jian surrendered; more than twenty bands of outlaws along the coast submitted or broke apart.

sentences.zh: 閏月，以武勝防禦使錢鏐為蘇杭觀察使。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, Wusheng defense commissioner Qian Liu was made Suzhou-Hangzhou observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, Qian Liu, defense commissioner of Wusheng, was made observation commissioner of Suzhou and Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 又以扈蹕都頭曹誠為黔中節度使，耀德都頭李鋋為鎮海節度使，宣威都頭孫惟晟為荊南節度使，六月，以捧日都頭陳珮為嶺南東道節度使，並同平章事。

translations.literal: Cao Cheng, chief of the Imperial Escort Guard, was made Qianzhong military governor; Li Chuan, chief of the Yaode Guard, was made Zhenhai military governor; Sun Weicheng, chief of the Xuanwei Guard, was made Jingnan military governor; in the sixth month, Chen Pei, chief of the Sun-support Guard, was made Lingnan East Circuit military governor—all with the additional title of Associate Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cheng of the Imperial Escort Guard was made military governor of Qianzhong; Li Chuan of the Yaode Guard, of Zhenhai; Sun Weicheng of the Xuanwei Guard, of Jingnan; and in the sixth month Chen Pei of the Sun-support Guard, of Lingnan East Circuit—each also named Associate Chief Minister.

sentences.zh: 時李茂貞跋扈，上以武臣難制，欲用諸王代之，占文城等四人皆加恩，解兵柄，令赴鎮。

translations.literal: At the time Li Maozhen was overbearing; the Emperor, finding military men hard to control, wished to replace them with imperial princes. Zhan Wencheng and three others were all favored with honors, stripped of military command, and ordered to their posts.
translations.idiomatic: Li Maozhen was then insolent and unchecked; believing martial men hard to govern, the Emperor meant to replace them with imperial princes. Zhan Wencheng and three others were honored, relieved of their commands, and sent to their circuits.

sentences.zh: 李匡籌出兵攻王鎔之樂壽、武強，以報殺匡威之恥。

translations.literal: Li Kuangchou sent troops to attack Wang Rong's Leshou and Wuqiang, to avenge the killing of Kuangwei.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kuangchou marched against Wang Rong's Leshou and Wuqiang to avenge his brother Kuangwei's death.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，王鎔遣兵救邢州；

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Wang Rong sent troops to relieve Xingzhou;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Wang Rong sent troops to relieve Xingzhou;

sentences.zh: 李克用敗之於平山，壬申，進擊鎮州。

translations.literal: Li Keyong defeated them at Pingshan; on the day renshen he pressed the attack on Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong routed them at Pingshan; on renshen he advanced on Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 鎔懼，請以兵糧二十萬助攻邢州，克用許之。

translations.literal: Rong, afraid, offered two hundred thousand in troops and supplies to join the assault on Xingzhou; Keyong agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Afraid, Rong offered two hundred thousand in men and grain to help take Xingzhou, and Keyong accepted.

sentences.zh: 克用治兵於欒城，合鎔兵三萬進屯任縣，李存信屯琉璃陂。

translations.literal: Keyong marshaled troops at Luancheng, combined with thirty thousand of Rong's men, and advanced to camp at Ren County; Li Cunxin encamped at Liuli Pond.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong mustered his army at Luancheng, joined Rong's thirty thousand men, and encamped at Ren County; Li Cunxin took position at Liuli Pond.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，楊行密克廬州，斬蔡儔。

translations.literal: On the day dinghai, Yang Xingmi took Luzhou and executed Cai Chou.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, Yang Xingmi captured Luzhou and beheaded Cai Chou.

sentences.zh: 左右請發儔父母塚，行密曰：「儔以此得罪，吾何為效之！」

translations.literal: Those around him asked to exhume the tombs of Chou's parents; Xingmi said: "Chou was condemned for this—why should I imitate him!"
translations.idiomatic: His attendants asked to open the graves of Chou's parents. Xingmi said, "Chou was condemned for such deeds—why should I copy him?"

sentences.zh: 加天雄節度使李茂莊同平章事。

translations.literal: Li Maozhuang, military governor of Tianxiong, was given the additional title of Associate Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Li Maozhuang, military governor of Tianxiong, was elevated to Associate Chief Minister.

sentences.zh: 錢鏐發民夫二十萬及十三都軍士築杭州羅城，周七十里。

translations.literal: Qian Liu mobilized two hundred thousand laborers and soldiers from thirteen commands to build Hangzhou's outer wall, seventy li in circumference.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu drafted two hundred thousand laborers and men from thirteen commands to raise Hangzhou's outer wall, seventy li around.

sentences.zh: 升州刺史張雄卒，馮弘鐸代之為刺史。

translations.literal: Shengzhou prefect Zhang Xiong died; Feng Hongduo replaced him as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Shengzhou prefect Zhang Xiong died, and Feng Hongduo succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 李茂貞恃功驕橫，上表及遺杜讓能書，辭語不遜。

translations.literal: Li Maozhen, trusting in his merits, grew proud and overbearing; in memorials and in letters to Du Rangneng his language was insolent.
translations.idiomatic: Li Maozhen, swollen with his own merits, grew arrogant; in memorials and in letters to Du Rangneng his words lacked all deference.

sentences.zh: 上怒，欲討之，茂貞又上表，略曰：「陛下貴為萬乘，不能庇元舅之一身；

translations.literal: The Emperor was angered and wished to campaign against him. Maozhen memorialized again, saying in part: "Your Majesty, exalted as lord of ten thousand chariots, could not shelter even one body of your mother's brother;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor raged and meant to punish him. Maozhen memorialized again, writing in part: "Your Majesty, sovereign of the realm, could not protect even your uncle's single life;

sentences.zh: 尊極九州，不能戮復恭之一豎。」

translations.literal: supreme over the nine regions, yet could not execute one petty eunuch of Fugong."
translations.idiomatic: master of the nine provinces, yet could not put to death one low eunuch of Fugong."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「今朝廷但觀強弱，不計是非。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Today the court looks only at strength and weakness, not at right and wrong."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "The court now weighs only power, never justice."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「約衰殘而行法，隨盛壯以加恩；

translations.literal: He also said: "It applies the law to the feeble and broken, and bestows favor as men grow strong and vigorous;
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "The law binds the weak and ruined, while favor follows the strong and thriving;

sentences.zh: 體物錙銖，看人衡纊。」

translations.literal: it measures things to the last ounce and weighs men by the thickness of their quilt."
translations.idiomatic: it counts every grain and measures every man's worth by the quilt on his bed."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「軍情易變，戎馬難羈，唯慮甸服生靈，因茲受禍，未審乘輿播越，自此何之！」

translations.literal: He also said: "Soldiers' hearts change easily; war-horses are hard to rein. I fear only that the people of the heartland will suffer calamity because of this—who knows where the imperial carriage, driven into exile, will go from here!"
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Armies turn fickle and steeds refuse the bridle. I fear only that the people of the heartland will suffer for this—who knows where the imperial carriage, cast into wandering exile, will go next!"

sentences.zh: 上益怒，決討茂貞，命杜讓能專掌其事，讓能諫曰：「陛下初臨大寶，國步末夷，茂貞近在國門，臣愚以為未宜與之構怨，萬一不克，悔之無及。」

translations.literal: The Emperor grew angrier still, resolved on campaigning against Maozhen, and ordered Du Rangneng to take sole charge of the matter. Rangneng remonstrated: "Your Majesty has but lately ascended the throne; the realm is not yet settled. Maozhen is close at the capital's gates. In my humble view it is not yet wise to make an enemy of him—if we fail, regret will come too late."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's wrath deepened; he resolved to strike Maozhen and put Du Rangneng in sole charge. Rangneng remonstrated: "Your Majesty has only lately taken the throne; the realm is not yet at peace. Maozhen sits near the capital. I think it unwise to pick this quarrel—fail, and there will be no undoing it."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「王室日卑，號令不出國門，此乃志士憤痛之秋。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "The royal house sinks day by day; decrees do not pass beyond the capital gates. This is the season for men of resolve to burn with grief.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "The throne weakens by the day; imperial orders no longer reach beyond the gate. This is the hour when loyal men should burn with shame.

sentences.zh: 藥弗瞑眩，厥疾弗瘳。

translations.literal: If the medicine does not dizzy the eyes, the illness will not be cured.
translations.idiomatic: No medicine works unless it first turns the head; no cure comes without pain.

sentences.zh: 朕不能甘心為孱懦之主，愔愔度日，坐視陵夷。

translations.literal: I cannot bear to be a feeble, timid sovereign, passing days in dull silence while watching decline.
translations.idiomatic: I will not content myself with a weak and craven reign, drifting day by day while the realm crumbles.

sentences.zh: 卿但為朕調兵食，朕自委諸王用兵，成敗不以責卿！」

translations.literal: You need only gather troops and provisions for me; I myself will entrust the princes with the campaign—success or failure shall not be laid to your charge!"
translations.idiomatic: You need only ready troops and grain for me; I shall commit the war to the princes—win or lose, the blame shall not fall on you!"

sentences.zh: 讓能曰：「陛下必欲行之，則中外大臣共宜協力以成聖志，不當獨以任臣。」

translations.literal: Rangneng said: "If Your Majesty is determined to proceed, then ministers within and without should all join forces to fulfill the sacred will—the burden should not fall on me alone."
translations.idiomatic: Rangneng said: "If Your Majesty insists, then every minister at court and in the provinces should share the burden—it should not rest on me alone."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿位居元輔，與朕同休戚，無宜避事！」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "You stand as chief minister, sharing my weal and woe—you ought not shirk the task!"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "You are chief minister; you share my fortune and my ruin—you must not shrink from this!"

sentences.zh: 讓能泣曰：「臣豈敢避事！

translations.literal: Rangneng wept and said: "How would your servant dare shirk the task!
translations.idiomatic: Rangneng wept: "How could I shirk it!

sentences.zh: 況陛下所欲行者，憲宗之志也；

translations.literal: Moreover, what Your Majesty wishes to do is Xianzong's own aspiration;
translations.idiomatic: What Your Majesty seeks is what Emperor Xianzong himself desired;

sentences.zh: 顧時有所未可，勢有所不能耳。

translations.literal: only the time was not yet right and the power not yet sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: only the hour was not ripe and the strength not yet at hand.

sentences.zh: 但恐他日臣徒受晁錯之誅，不能弭七國之禍也。

translations.literal: I fear only that one day your servant will suffer execution like Chao Cuo yet fail to quell the calamity of the Seven Kingdoms.
translations.idiomatic: I fear only that I shall die like Chao Cuo and still fail to still the rebellion of the Seven Kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 敢不奉詔，以死繼之！」

translations.literal: Yet how dare I not obey the edict—I shall follow it even unto death!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet how can I refuse? I obey, and will follow even unto death!"

sentences.zh: 上乃命讓能留中書，計畫調度，月餘不歸。

translations.literal: The Emperor then ordered Rangneng to remain at the Secretariat, planning and dispatching supplies; for more than a month he did not return home.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Rangneng to remain at the Secretariat to plan and provision the campaign; for more than a month he did not go home.

sentences.zh: 崔昭緯陰結邠、岐，為之耳目，讓能朝發一言，二鎮夕必知之。

translations.literal: Cui Zhaowei secretly allied with Bin and Qi, serving as their eyes and ears; a word Rangneng spoke at court in the morning the two commands knew by evening.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zhaowei secretly colluded with Bin and Qi and served as their spy; whatever Rangneng said at court by morning the two commands knew by night.

sentences.zh: 李茂貞使其黨糾合市人數百千人，擁觀軍容使西門君遂馬訴曰：「岐帥無罪，不宜致討，使百姓塗炭。」

translations.literal: Li Maozhen had his partisans gather several hundred or thousand townspeople, surround Army Appearance Commissioner Ximen Junsui on horseback, and petition: "The Qi commander is guiltless and ought not be attacked—do not bring torment upon the common people."
translations.idiomatic: Li Maozhen's agents rallied hundreds and thousands of townspeople, surrounded Army Appearance Commissioner Ximen Junsui on horseback, and cried: "The commander of Qi is innocent—do not make war on him and burn the people alive."

sentences.zh: 君遂曰：「此宰相事，非吾所及。」

translations.literal: Junsui said: "This is the chancellor's affair—it is not within my reach."
translations.idiomatic: Junsui answered: "That is the chancellor's business, not mine."

sentences.zh: 市人又邀崔昭緯、鄭延昌肩輿訴之，二相曰：「茲事主上專委杜太尉，吾曹不預知。」

translations.literal: The townspeople then stopped Cui Zhaowei and Zheng Yanchang in their palanquins to petition them; the two chancellors said: "On this matter His Majesty has entrusted Grand Marshal Du alone—we were not consulted beforehand."
translations.idiomatic: The mob then waylaid Cui Zhaowei and Zheng Yanchang in their palanquins. The two chancellors said: "The Emperor has entrusted this solely to Grand Marshal Du—we knew nothing of it."

sentences.zh: 市人因亂投瓦石，二相下輿走匿民家，僅自免，喪堂印及朝服。

translations.literal: The townspeople in the tumult threw tiles and stones; the two chancellors left their palanquins and fled into common houses, barely escaping with their lives, and lost their hall seals and court robes.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd pelted them with tiles and stones; the two chancellors abandoned their palanquins and hid in common houses, barely escaping with their lives and losing their seals and court robes.

sentences.zh: 上命捕其唱帥者誅之，用兵之意益堅。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered the ringleaders seized and executed; his resolve to use force grew all the firmer.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered the ringleaders arrested and killed; his determination to march only hardened.

sentences.zh: 京師民或亡匿山谷，嚴刑所不能禁。

translations.literal: People of the capital fled into mountain valleys; harsh punishments could not stop them.
translations.idiomatic: People of the capital fled into the hills; even harsh punishment could not stop them.

sentences.zh: 八月，以嗣覃王嗣周為京西招討使，神策大將軍李金歲副之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Imperial Prince Sizhou of Tan was made Western Capital campaign commander, with Divine Strategy General Li Jinsui as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Imperial Prince Sizhou of Tan was made commander of the Western Capital campaign, with Divine Strategy General Li Jinsui as his second.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，楊行密遣田頵將宣州兵二萬攻歙州；

translations.literal: On the day bingchen, Yang Xingmi sent Tian Jun with twenty thousand troops from Xuanzhou to attack Shezhou;
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, Yang Xingmi sent Tian Jun with twenty thousand Xuanzhou troops against Shezhou;

sentences.zh: 歙州刺史裴樞城守，久不下。

translations.literal: Shezhou prefect Pei Shu held the city; for long it would not fall.
translations.idiomatic: Shezhou prefect Pei Shu held the walls, and for long the city would not fall.

sentences.zh: 時諸將為刺史者多貪暴，獨池州團練使陶雅寬厚得民，歙人曰：「得陶雅為刺史，請聽命。」

translations.literal: At the time many generals serving as prefects were greedy and brutal; only Chizhou training commissioner Tao Ya was generous and won the people. The men of She said: "If we may have Tao Ya as prefect, we will submit."
translations.idiomatic: Many generals then holding prefectures were greedy and cruel; only Chizhou training commissioner Tao Ya was generous and beloved. The people of She said, "Make Tao Ya our prefect, and we will obey."

sentences.zh: 行密即以雅為歙州刺史，歙人納之。

translations.literal: Xingmi thereupon appointed Ya prefect of Shezhou, and the people of She submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi made Ya prefect of Shezhou, and the people of She submitted.

sentences.zh: 雅盡禮見樞，送之還朝。

translations.literal: Ya received Shu with full courtesy and sent him back to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Ya treated Shu with full courtesy and sent him back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 樞，遵慶之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Shu was a great-grandson of Pei Zunqing.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was a great-grandson of Pei Zunqing.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠命龐師古移兵攻兗州，與朱瑾戰，屢破之。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong ordered Pang Shigu to shift troops and attack Yanzhou, fighting Zhu Jin and repeatedly defeating him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong ordered Pang Shigu against Yanzhou; he fought Zhu Jin and beat him again and again.

sentences.zh: 九月，丁卯，以錢鏐為鎮海節度使。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day dingmao, Qian Liu was appointed military governor of Zhenhai.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on dingmao, Qian Liu was made military governor of Zhenhai.

sentences.zh: 李存孝夜犯李存信營，虜奉誠軍使孫考老。

translations.literal: Li Cunxiao by night raided Li Cunxin's camp and captured Sun Kaolao, commissioner of Fengcheng Army.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunxiao raided Li Cunxin's camp by night and captured Fengcheng commissioner Sun Kaolao.

sentences.zh: 李克用自引兵攻邢州，掘塹築壘環之。

translations.literal: Li Keyong personally led troops to attack Xingzhou, digging moats and building stockades around it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong personally besieged Xingzhou, digging trenches and building stockades all around.

sentences.zh: 存孝時出兵突擊，塹壘不能成。

translations.literal: Cunxiao from time to time sallied to strike, and the moats and stockades could not be completed.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxiao sallied repeatedly and the trenches and walls could not be finished.

sentences.zh: 河東牙將袁奉韜密使人謂存孝曰：「大王惟俟塹成即歸晉陽，尚書所憚者獨大王耳，諸將非尚書敵也。

translations.literal: Hedong staff officer Yuan Fengtao secretly sent someone to tell Cunxiao: "The Prince waits only for the moats to be finished and then returns to Jinyang. The Minister fears only you; the other generals are no match for him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Fengtao secretly told Cunxiao: "The Prince will return to Jinyang once the trenches are done. He fears only you—the other generals are nothing to him.

sentences.zh: 大王若歸，咫尺之塹，安能沮尚書之鋒銳邪！」

translations.literal: If you return, how can trenches a foot away block the Minister's sharp advance!"
translations.idiomatic: If you leave, how will a shallow ditch stop his assault?"

sentences.zh: 存孝以為然，按兵不出。

translations.literal: Cunxiao thought this correct and held his troops without sallying.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxiao believed him and kept his men in camp.

sentences.zh: 旬日，塹壘成，飛走不能越，存孝由是遂窮。

translations.literal: Within ten days the moats and stockades were complete; neither bird nor beast could cross, and Cunxiao was thereby brought to extremity.
translations.idiomatic: In ten days the works were done; nothing could cross, and Cunxiao was trapped.

sentences.zh: 汴將鄧季筠從克用攻邢州，輕騎逃歸。

translations.literal: Bian general Deng Jiyun, who had followed Keyong against Xingzhou, fled back on light horse.
translations.idiomatic: Bian general Deng Jiyun, serving under Keyong at Xingzhou, fled home on a fast horse.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠大喜，使將親軍。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong was greatly pleased and had him command his personal guard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong was delighted and put him in command of his personal guard.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，覃王嗣周帥禁軍三萬送鳳翔節度使徐彥若赴鎮，軍於興平。

translations.literal: On the day yihai, Imperial Prince Sizhou of Tan led thirty thousand imperial guards to escort Fengxiang military governor Xu Yanruo to his post, encamping at Xingping.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, Prince Sizhou led thirty thousand guards to escort Xu Yanruo to Fengxiang and camped at Xingping.

sentences.zh: 李茂貞、王行瑜合兵近六萬，軍於盩厔以拒之。

translations.literal: Li Maozhen and Wang Xingyu combined nearly sixty thousand troops and encamped at Zhouzhi to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Maozhen and Wang Xingyu massed nearly sixty thousand men at Zhouzhi to block them.

sentences.zh: 禁軍皆新募市井少年，茂貞、行瑜所將皆邊兵百戰之餘，壬午，茂貞等進逼興平，禁軍皆望風逃潰，茂貞等乘勝進攻三橋，京城大震，士民奔散，市人復守闕請誅首議用兵者。

translations.literal: The imperial guards were all newly recruited youths from the markets; those led by Maozhen and Xingyu were frontier soldiers seasoned in a hundred battles. On the day renwu, Maozhen and the others pressed close to Xingping; the imperial guards fled at the mere sight of them. Maozhen and the others pressed their victory to attack the Three Bridges; the capital was greatly shaken, officials and people scattered, and townspeople again guarded the palace gates demanding execution of those who had first urged war.
translations.idiomatic: The guards were raw recruits from the streets; Maozhen and Xingyu led hardened frontier veterans. On renwu they pressed Xingping; the guards broke and fled. Victorious, they stormed the Three Bridges. The capital panicked; crowds again besieged the palace demanding the heads of those who had urged war.

sentences.zh: 崔昭緯心害太尉、門下侍郎、同平章事杜讓能，密遺茂貞書曰：「用兵非主上意，皆出於杜太尉耳。」

translations.literal: Cui Zhaowei bore malice toward Grand Marshal and Vice Director of the Secretariat Du Rangneng and secretly sent Maozhen a letter saying: "The use of troops is not the sovereign's intent—it all comes from Grand Marshal Du."
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zhaowei hated Du Rangneng and secretly wrote Maozhen: "The Emperor did not want this war—it was all Du Rangneng's doing."

sentences.zh: 甲申，茂貞陳於臨皋驛，表讓能罪，請誅之。

translations.literal: On the day jiashen, Maozhen drew up his forces at Lingao Post Station, memorialized Rangneng's crimes, and requested his execution.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, Maozhen camped at Lingao Station, listed Rangneng's crimes, and demanded his death.

sentences.zh: 讓能言於上曰：「臣固先言之矣，請以臣為解。」

translations.literal: Rangneng said to the Emperor: "Your servant spoke of this beforehand. I beg that your servant be the settlement."
translations.idiomatic: Rangneng told the Emperor, "I warned you of this. Take me as the sacrifice."

sentences.zh: 上涕下不自禁，曰：「與卿訣矣！」

translations.literal: The Emperor's tears flowed unchecked as he said: "I take leave of you!"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wept uncontrollably: "This is our farewell!"

sentences.zh: 是日，貶讓能梧州刺史，制辭略曰：「棄卿士之臧謀，構籓垣之深釁，咨詢之際，證執彌堅。」

translations.literal: That day Rangneng was demoted to prefect of Wuzhou. The edict text said in part: "He abandoned the good counsel of ministers and engineered deep enmity with the frontier commands; when consulted, his obstinacy grew all the firmer."
translations.idiomatic: That day Rangneng was demoted to Wuzhou. The edict read in part: "He spurned wise counsel and provoked the frontier lords; when questioned, he only grew more stubborn."

sentences.zh: 又流觀軍容使西門君遂於儋州，內樞密使李周潼於崖州，段詡於歡州。

translations.literal: Ximen Junsui, Army Appearance Commissioner, was exiled to Danzhou; Li Zhoutong, Inner Palace Secretariat Commissioner, to Yazhou; and Duan Xu to Huanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Army Appearance Commissioner Ximen Junsui was exiled to Danzhou; Inner Secretariat Commissioner Li Zhoutong to Yazhou; Duan Xu to Huanzhou.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，上御安福門，斬君遂、周潼、詡，再貶讓能雷州司戶。

translations.literal: On the day yiyou, the Emperor attended the Anfu Gate, beheaded Junsui, Zhoutong, and Xu, and again demoted Rangneng to revenue clerk of Leizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, the Emperor at the Anfu Gate beheaded Junsui, Zhoutong, and Xu and demoted Rangneng again to clerk of Leizhou.

sentences.zh: 遣使謂茂貞曰：「惑朕舉兵者，三人也，非讓能之罪。」

translations.literal: He sent envoys to tell Maozhen: "Those who misled Us into raising troops were three men—not Rangneng's crime."
translations.idiomatic: He sent word to Maozhen: "Three men misled me into war—not Rangneng."

sentences.zh: 以內侍駱全瓘、劉景宣為左右軍中尉。

translations.literal: The inner attendants Luo Quanjin and Liu Jingxuan were appointed Left and Right Army Supervising Commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Inner attendants Luo Quanjin and Liu Jingxuan were made Left and Right Army commissioners.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，以東都留守韋昭度為司徒、門下侍郎、同平章事，御史中丞崔胤為戶部侍郎、同平章事，胤，慎由之子也，外寬弘而內巧險，與崔昭緯深相結，故得為相。

translations.literal: On the day renchen, Wei Zhaodu, Eastern Capital regent, was made Grand Master, Vice Director of the Secretariat, and Associate Chief Minister; Cui Yin, Vice Censor-in-Chief, was made Vice Minister of Revenue and Associate Chief Minister. Yin was a son of Cui Shenyou—outwardly broad and tolerant, inwardly crafty and dangerous; deeply allied with Cui Zhaowei, he thereby attained the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, Wei Zhaodu became Grand Master and Associate Chief Minister; Cui Yin, son of Cui Shenyou, became Associate Chief Minister as well. Outwardly genial, inwardly treacherous, Yin was Zhaowei's ally and thus rose to the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 季父安潛謂所親曰：「吾父兄刻苦以立門戶，終為緇郎所壞！」

translations.literal: His uncle An Qian said to those close to him: "Our fathers and brothers toiled to raise this house—it will be ruined by the Silk Lord at last!"
translations.idiomatic: His uncle An Qian said to friends: "Our family built its name through hardship—now the Silk Lord will destroy it!"

sentences.zh: 緇郎，胤小字也。

translations.literal: Silk Lord" was Yin's childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: Silk Lord" was Yin's childhood name.

sentences.zh: 李茂貞勒兵不解，請誅杜讓能然後還鎮，崔昭緯復從而擠之。

translations.literal: Li Maozhen held his troops without dispersing, demanding that Du Rangneng be executed before he would return to his command; Cui Zhaowei again pressed the attack from within.
translations.idiomatic: Li Maozhen refused to withdraw until Rangneng was dead; Cui Zhaowei pressed the case again.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，賜讓能及其弟戶部侍郎弘徽自盡。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Rangneng and his younger brother Honghui, Vice Minister of Revenue, were granted permission to take their own lives.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, Rangneng and his brother Honghui were ordered to kill themselves.

sentences.zh: 復下詔佈告中外，稱「讓能舉枉錯直，愛憎繫於一時；

translations.literal: An edict was again issued to proclaim throughout within and without, stating: "Rangneng upheld the crooked and wronged the straight; love and hate hung on the moment;
translations.idiomatic: A new edict proclaimed: "Rangneng upheld the wicked and wronged the upright; favor and spite ruled the hour;

sentences.zh: 鬻獄賣官，聚斂逾於巨萬。」

translations.literal: he sold justice and traded offices, amassing more than tens of thousands in wealth."
translations.idiomatic: he sold offices and judgments and amassed fortunes beyond counting."

sentences.zh: 自是朝廷動息皆稟於邠、岐，南、北司往往依附二鎮以邀恩澤。

translations.literal: From then on every movement and rest of the court awaited Bin and Qi; the southern and northern palace offices often attached themselves to the two commands to seek favor.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth the court's every move awaited Bin and Qi; palace offices north and south courted the two warlords for favor.

sentences.zh: 有崔鋋、王超者，為二鎮判官，凡天子有所可否，其不逞者，輒訴於鋋、超，二人則教茂貞、行瑜上章論之，朝廷少有依違，其辭語已不遜。

translations.literal: Cui Chan and Wang Chao served as staff judges for the two commands. Whenever the Son of Heaven approved or denied something, those who were discontented would appeal to Chan and Chao; the two would then instruct Maozhen and Xingyu to memorialize on the matter. If the court showed the slightest hesitation, their language was already insolent.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Chan and Wang Chao were staff judges for the two commands. Disgruntled parties appealed to them; they coached Maozhen and Xingyu to memorialize. If the court wavered, their language turned insolent.

sentences.zh: 制復以茂貞為鳳翔節度使兼山南西道節度使、守中書令，於是茂貞盡有鳳翔、興元、洋、隴秦等十五州之地。

translations.literal: An edict again appointed Maozhen military governor of Fengxiang and concurrently of Shannan West, holding the Secretariat seal; Maozhen thereby held altogether fifteen prefectures including Fengxiang, Xingyuan, Yang, Long, and Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen was again made governor of Fengxiang and Shannan West and Keeper of the Secretariat Seal; he now held fifteen prefectures including Fengxiang, Xingyuan, Yang, Long, and Qin.

sentences.zh: 以徐彥若為御史大夫。

translations.literal: Xu Yanruo was appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yanruo was made Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，以泉州刺史王潮為福建觀察使。

translations.literal: On the day wuxu, Wang Chao, prefect of Quanzhou, was made Fujian observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, Wang Chao of Quanzhou was made Fujian observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 舒州刺史倪章棄城走，楊行密以李神福為舒州刺史。

translations.literal: Ni Zhang, prefect of Shuzhou, abandoned the city and fled; Yang Xingmi appointed Li Shenfu prefect of Shuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ni Zhang of Shuzhou fled; Yang Xingmi made Li Shenfu prefect.

sentences.zh: 邠寧節度使、守侍中兼中書令王行瑜求為尚書令；

translations.literal: Wang Xingyu, military governor of Binning, Palace Attendant, and Keeper of the Secretariat Seal, requested appointment as Director of the Department of State Affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Binning governor Wang Xingyu, Palace Attendant and Keeper of the Secretariat Seal, asked to be made Director of the Department of State Affairs;

sentences.zh: 韋昭度密奏：「太宗以尚書令執政，遂登大位，自是不以授人臣。

translations.literal: Wei Zhaodu secretly memorialized: "Taizong governed as Director of the Department of State Affairs and thereafter ascended the throne; since then the post has not been granted to subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhaodu secretly wrote: "Taizong held that office and became emperor; since then it has not been given to a subject.

sentences.zh: 惟郭子儀以大功拜尚書令，終身避讓。

translations.literal: Only Guo Ziyi, for great merit, was appointed Director of the Department of State Affairs, yet he declined it all his life.
translations.idiomatic: Only Guo Ziyi received it for supreme merit—and declined it for life.

sentences.zh: 行瑜安可輕議！」

translations.literal: How can Xingyu be lightly discussed for it!"
translations.idiomatic: Xingyu must not even be considered!"

sentences.zh: 十一月，以行瑜為太師，賜號尚父，仍賜鐵券。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Xingyu was made Grand Preceptor, granted the title Exalted Father, and given an iron certificate of mercy.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Xingyu was made Grand Preceptor, styled Exalted Father, and given an iron certificate.

sentences.zh: 十二月，朱全忠請徙鹽鐵於汴州以便供軍；

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Zhu Quanzhong requested that the Salt and Iron Commission be moved to Bianzhou to ease supply for the army;
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Zhu Quanzhong asked to move the Salt and Iron Commission to Bianzhou to supply his army;

sentences.zh: 崔昭緯為全忠新破徐、鄆，兵力倍增，若更判鹽鐵，不可複製，乃賜詔開諭之。

translations.literal: Cui Zhaowei argued that Quanzhong, having newly broken Xu and Yan, had doubled his military strength; if he also controlled Salt and Iron he could not be restrained, and so an edict was issued to instruct and persuade him.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zhaowei argued that with Xu and Yan conquered, Quanzhong's power had doubled; giving him Salt and Iron would make him uncontrollable, and an edict was sent to dissuade him.

sentences.zh: 汴將葛從周攻齊州刺史朱威，朱瑄、朱瑾引兵救之。

translations.literal: Bian general Ge Congzhou attacked Qizhou prefect Zhu Wei; Zhu Xuan and Zhu Jin led troops to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Bian general Ge Congzhou attacked Zhu Wei of Qizhou; Zhu Xuan and Zhu Jin marched to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 初，武安節度使周岳殺閔勖，據潭州，邵州刺史鄧處訥聞而哭之，諸將入吊，處訥曰：「吾與公等鹹受僕射大恩，今周岳無狀殺之，吾欲與公等竭一州之力，為僕射報仇，可乎？」

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhou Yue, military governor of Wu'an, had killed Min Xu and seized Tanzhou. Deng Chuna, prefect of Shaozhou, wept on hearing it. When the generals came to condole, Chuna said: "You and I alike received great kindness from the Vice Director. Now Zhou Yue has killed him without cause. I wish to exhaust the strength of one prefecture with you to avenge the Vice Director—will you?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yue of Wu'an had killed Min Xu and seized Tanzhou. Deng Chuna of Shaozhou wept. When his officers came to mourn, he said: "We all owed the Vice Director a great debt. Zhou Yue murdered him. Will you help me spend this prefecture's strength to avenge him?"

sentences.zh: 皆曰：「善！」

translations.literal: All said: "Good!"
translations.idiomatic: All said: "Yes!"

sentences.zh: 於是訓卒厲兵，八年，乃結朗州刺史雷滿共攻潭州，克之，斬岳，自稱留後。

translations.literal: Thereupon they trained soldiers and sharpened weapons; after eight years they joined Lei Man, prefect of Langzhou, to attack Tanzhou together, took it, beheaded Yue, and Chuna styled himself acting regent.
translations.idiomatic: They drilled troops and sharpened weapons. Eight years later, with Langzhou prefect Lei Man, they took Tanzhou, killed Yue, and Chuna declared himself acting regent.

sentences.zh: 昭宗聖穆景文孝皇帝上之中乾寧元年（

translations.literal: First year of the Qianning era of Emperor Zhaozong, the Sagacious, Reverent, Cultivated, and Filial, upper fascicle, middle section (
translations.idiomatic: First year of the Qianning era of Emperor Zhaozong (upper fascicle, middle section) (

sentences.zh: 甲寅，公元八九四年）

translations.literal: jiayin, corresponding to the year 894 CE)
translations.idiomatic: the year jiayin, equivalent to 894 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙丑朔，赦天下，改元。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the yichou new moon, a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm and the era name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the yichou new moon, the court proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name.

sentences.zh: 李茂貞入朝，大陳兵自衛，數日歸鎮。

translations.literal: Li Maozhen came to court, displayed his troops in great array for self-protection, and after several days returned to his command.
translations.idiomatic: Li Maozhen came to court with a great armed escort and returned to his command after several days.

sentences.zh: 以李匡籌為盧龍節度使。

translations.literal: Li Kuangchou was appointed military governor of Lulong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kuangchou was made military governor of Lulong.

sentences.zh: 二月，朱全忠自將擊朱瑄，軍於魚山。

translations.literal: In the second month, Zhu Quanzhong personally led troops against Zhu Xuan, encamping at Mount Yu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Zhu Quanzhong personally marched against Zhu Xuan and camped at Mount Yu.

sentences.zh: 瑄與瑾合兵攻之，兗、鄆兵大敗，死者萬餘人。

translations.literal: Xuan and Jin combined forces to attack him; the Yan and Yanzhou armies were utterly defeated, with more than ten thousand dead.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan and Jin joined against him; the Yan armies were shattered with more than ten thousand dead.

sentences.zh: 以右散騎常侍鄭綮為禮部侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: Zheng Yin, Right Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, was appointed Vice Minister of Rites and Associate Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yin, Right Attendant of the Cavalry, was made Vice Minister of Rites and Associate Chief Minister.

sentences.zh: 綮好詼諧，多為歇後詩，譏嘲時事；

translations.literal: Yin loved wit and often wrote "tail-clipped" poems mocking current affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Yin loved humor and wrote clipped-tail poems mocking the times;

sentences.zh: 上以為有所蘊，手注班簿，命以為相，聞者大驚。

translations.literal: the Emperor thought he had hidden depth, personally annotated the roster of officials, and ordered him made chancellor; hearers were greatly astonished.
translations.idiomatic: the Emperor thought him deep, marked the roster himself, and named him chancellor; all were astonished.

sentences.zh: 堂吏往告之，綮笑曰：「諸君大誤，使天下更無人，未至鄭綮！」

translations.literal: A clerk of the Secretariat went to inform him. Yin laughed and said: "You gentlemen are greatly mistaken—even if the realm had no other men, it would not yet come to Zheng Yin!"
translations.idiomatic: A clerk told him. Yin laughed: "You are mistaken—even if the world were empty of men, it would not yet be Zheng Yin's turn!"

sentences.zh: 史曰：「特出聖意。」

translations.literal: The clerk said: "It is solely the sacred will."
translations.idiomatic: The clerk said: "It is the Emperor's own choice."

sentences.zh: 綮曰：「果如是，奈人笑何！」

translations.literal: Yin said: "If it is truly so, what can be done about men's laughter!"
translations.idiomatic: Yin said: "If so, how shall we bear men's laughter!"

sentences.zh: 既而賀客至，綮搔首言曰：「歇後鄭五作宰相，時事可知矣！」

translations.literal: Presently congratulatory guests arrived. Yin scratched his head and said: "Tail-clipped Zheng Five made chancellor—the times can be known from that!"
translations.idiomatic: When guests came to congratulate, Yin scratched his head: "Tail-clipped Zheng Five is chancellor—the age tells its own tale!"

sentences.zh: 累讓不獲，乃視事。

translations.literal: He declined repeatedly without success and then took up office.
translations.idiomatic: He declined in vain and took office.

sentences.zh: 以邵州刺史鄧處訥為武安節度使。

translations.literal: Deng Chuna, prefect of Shaozhou, was appointed military governor of Wu'an.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Chuna of Shaozhou was made military governor of Wu'an.

sentences.zh: 彰義節度使張鈞薨，表其兄鐇為留後。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun, military governor of Zhangyi, died; he memorialized that his elder brother Zheng be acting regent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun of Zhangyi died; he had asked that his brother Zheng succeed him.

sentences.zh: 三月，黃州刺史吳討舉州降楊行密。

translations.literal: In the third month, Wu Tao, prefect of Huangzhou, surrendered his prefecture to Yang Xingmi.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Wu Tao of Huangzhou surrendered to Yang Xingmi.

sentences.zh: 邢州城中食盡，甲申，李存孝登城謂李克用曰：「兒蒙王恩得富貴，苟非困於讒慝，安肯捨父子而從仇讎乎！

translations.literal: Food in Xingzhou city was exhausted. On the day jiashen, Li Cunxiao mounted the wall and said to Li Keyong: "Your son received the Prince's grace and won wealth and rank. Had he not been trapped by slander, how would he have abandoned father and son to follow an enemy!
translations.idiomatic: Xingzhou starved. On jiashen, Li Cunxiao stood on the wall and told Li Keyong: "I owed you everything. Only slander drove me to betray you for our enemies!

sentences.zh: 願一見王，死不恨！」

translations.literal: I wish only to see the Prince once—then death will hold no regret!"
translations.idiomatic: Let me see you once more—then I can die without regret!"

sentences.zh: 克用使劉夫人視之。

translations.literal: Keyong sent Lady Liu to see him.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong sent Lady Liu to see him.

sentences.zh: 夫人引存孝出見克用，存孝泥首謝罪曰：「兒粗立微勞，存信逼兒，失圖至此！」

translations.literal: The lady led Cunxiao out to see Keyong. Cunxiao pressed his face in the dust and begged forgiveness: "Your son won slight merit; Cunxin pressed him, and he lost his way to this!"
translations.idiomatic: She brought Cunxiao out. He pressed his face to the earth: "I won some merit; Cunxin drove me to this ruin!"

sentences.zh: 克用叱之曰：「汝遺朱全忠、王鎔書，毀我萬端，亦存信教汝乎！」

translations.literal: Keyong shouted at him: "You sent letters to Zhu Quanzhong and Wang Rong slandering me in ten thousand ways—did Cunxin teach you that too!"
translations.idiomatic: Keyong roared: "You wrote Zhu Quanzhong and Wang Rong vilifying me in every way—did Cunxin teach you that as well?"

sentences.zh: 囚之，歸於晉陽，車裂於牙門。

translations.literal: He was imprisoned, taken to Jinyang, and torn apart by chariots at the headquarters gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was imprisoned, taken to Jinyang, and torn apart by chariots at headquarters.

sentences.zh: 存孝驍勇，克用軍中皆莫及；

translations.literal: Cunxiao was fierce and brave; in Keyong's army none could match him;
translations.idiomatic: Cunxiao was matchlessly brave; none in Keyong's army equaled him;

sentences.zh: 常將騎兵為先鋒，所向無敵，身被重鎧，腰弓髀槊，獨舞鐵□陷陳，萬人辟易。

translations.literal: he often led cavalry as vanguard, invincible wherever he went, clad in heavy armor with bow at waist and spear at thigh, charging alone with iron spear into the battle line while ten thousand gave way.
translations.idiomatic: he led the vanguard horse, invincible in every fight, in heavy mail with bow and thigh spear, charging alone with an iron lance while ten thousand gave way.

sentences.zh: 每以二馬自隨，馬稍乏，就陣中易之，出入如飛。

translations.literal: He always kept two horses with him; when one tired he exchanged it in the press of battle and came and went like flight.
translations.idiomatic: He kept two horses; when one tired he swapped mounts in the battle line and moved like the wind.

sentences.zh: 克用惜其才，意臨刑諸將必為之請，因而釋之。

translations.literal: Keyong prized his talent and expected that at execution the generals would surely plead for him and he would then release him.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong valued his talent and expected his generals to plead for him at the last hour.

sentences.zh: 既而諸將疾其能，竟無一人言者。

translations.literal: But the generals envied his ability, and in the end not one spoke.
translations.idiomatic: But the generals envied him, and not one spoke up.

sentences.zh: 既死，克用為之不視事者旬日，私恨諸將，而於李存信竟無所譴。

translations.literal: After his death Keyong for ten days did not attend to affairs, privately resenting the generals, yet he punished Li Cunxin not at all.
translations.idiomatic: After his death Keyong refused audiences for ten days and privately resented his generals, yet never punished Li Cunxin.

sentences.zh: 又有薛阿檀者，其勇與存孝相侔，諸將疾之，常不得志，密與存孝通；

translations.literal: There was also Xue Atan, whose courage matched Cunxiao's; the generals envied him and he often found no satisfaction, secretly communicating with Cunxiao;
translations.idiomatic: Xue Atan was Cunxiao's equal in valor; the generals envied him and he secretly kept in touch with Cunxiao;

sentences.zh: 存孝誅，恐事洩，遂自殺。

translations.literal: when Cunxiao was executed, fearing exposure, he took his own life.
translations.idiomatic: when Cunxiao died, fearing exposure, he killed himself.

sentences.zh: 自是克用兵勢浸弱，而朱全忠獨盛矣。

translations.literal: From then on Keyong's military power gradually weakened, while Zhu Quanzhong alone grew mighty.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Keyong's power waned while Zhu Quanzhong alone grew supreme.

sentences.zh: 克用表馬師素為邢洺節度使。

translations.literal: Keyong memorialized that Ma Shisu be military governor of Xing and Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong made Ma Shisu governor of Xing and Ming.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠遣軍將張從晦慰撫壽州。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong sent army officer Zhang Conghui to comfort and reassure Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong sent Zhang Conghui to reassure Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 從晦陵侮刺史江彥溫而與諸將夜飲；

translations.literal: Conghui treated prefect Jiang Yanwen with contempt and drank at night with the generals;
translations.idiomatic: Conghui insulted Prefect Jiang Yanwen and drank with the officers at night;

sentences.zh: 彥溫疑其謀己，明日，盡殺在席諸將，以書謝全忠而自殺。

translations.literal: Yanwen suspected a plot against himself; the next day he killed all the generals at the table, wrote Quanzhong a letter of apology, and killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yanwen feared a plot; next day he killed every officer at the table, wrote Quanzhong to apologize, and killed himself.

sentences.zh: 軍中推其子從頊知軍州事，全忠為之腰斬從晦。

translations.literal: The army made his son Congxu acting military commissioner; Quanzhong had Conghui cut in two at the waist for it.
translations.idiomatic: The army made his son Congxu commissioner; Quanzhong had Conghui cut in half at the waist.

sentences.zh: 五月，加鎮海節度使錢鏐同平章事。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Qian Liu, military governor of Zhenhai, was given the additional title of Associate Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Qian Liu of Zhenhai was made Associate Chief Minister.

sentences.zh: 劉建鋒、馬殷引兵至澧陵，鄧處訥遣邵州指揮使蔣勳、鄧繼崇將步騎三千守龍回關。

translations.literal: Liu Jianfeng and Ma Yin led troops to Liling. Deng Chuna sent Shaozhou commanders Jiang Xun and Deng Jichong with three thousand foot and horse to hold Longhui Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jianfeng and Ma Yin reached Liling. Deng Chuna sent Jiang Xun and Deng Jichong with three thousand men to hold Longhui Pass.

sentences.zh: 殷先至關下，遣使詣勳，勳等以牛酒犒師。

translations.literal: Yin arrived first below the pass and sent envoys to Xun; Xun and the others feasted the army with cattle and wine.
translations.idiomatic: Yin arrived first and sent envoys; Xun and the others feasted his army.

sentences.zh: 殷使說勳曰：「劉驤智勇兼人，術家言當興翼、軫間。

translations.literal: Yin had someone persuade Xun, saying: "Liu Jianfeng combines wisdom and courage; diviners say he will rise between the Wings and the Chariot constellations.
translations.idiomatic: Yin sent a persuader: "Liu Jianfeng is wise and brave; diviners say he will rise between the Wings and the Chariot.

sentences.zh: 今將十萬眾，精銳無敵，而君以鄉兵數千拒之，難矣。

translations.literal: Now he leads a hundred thousand, elite and unmatched, while you resist with a few thousand local troops—how hard that will be.
translations.idiomatic: He brings a hundred thousand elite men, and you mean to stop him with a few thousand local troops?

sentences.zh: 不如先下之，取富貴，還鄉里，不亦善乎！」

translations.literal: Better to submit first, win wealth and rank, and return home—is that not good!"
translations.idiomatic: Submit now, win rank and riches, and go home—would that not be better?"

sentences.zh: 勳等然之，謂眾曰：「東軍許吾屬還。」

translations.literal: Xun and the others agreed and told the crowd: "The eastern army promises us we may return."
translations.idiomatic: Xun agreed and told his men: "The eastern army promises we may go home."

sentences.zh: 士卒皆歡呼，棄旗幟鎧仗遁去。

translations.literal: The soldiers all shouted for joy, cast down banners, armor, and weapons, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers cheered, threw down their arms, and fled.

sentences.zh: 建鋒令前鋒衣其甲，張其旗，趨潭州。

translations.literal: Jianfeng ordered the vanguard to wear their armor and raise their banners and hurry to Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jianfeng had his vanguard wear their armor, raise their banners, and march on Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 潭人以為邵州兵還，不為備。

translations.literal: The people of Tan thought Shaozhou troops were returning and made no preparation.
translations.idiomatic: Tanzhou thought Shaozhou troops were returning and took no precautions.

sentences.zh: 建鋒入徑入府，處訥方宴，擒斬之。

translations.literal: Jianfeng went straight into the headquarters; Chuna was at banquet and was seized and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Jianfeng walked straight into headquarters; Chuna was feasting and was seized and beheaded.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，建鋒潭州，自稱留後。

translations.literal: On the day wuchen, Jianfeng held Tanzhou and styled himself acting regent.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, Jianfeng held Tanzhou and declared himself acting regent.

sentences.zh: 王建攻彭州，城中人相食，彭州內外都指揮使趙章出降。

translations.literal: Wang Jian attacked Pengzhou; within the city people ate one another. Zhao Zhang, supreme commander inside and outside Pengzhou, came out and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian pressed Pengzhou; inside the walls people ate the dead. Zhao Zhang, commander of Pengzhou, surrendered.

sentences.zh: 王先成請築龍尾道，屬於女牆。

translations.literal: Wang Xiancheng requested construction of a Dragon Tail ramp attached to the parapet.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiancheng asked to build a Dragon Tail ramp up to the battlements.

sentences.zh: 丙子，西川兵登城，楊晟猶帥眾力戰，刀子都虞候王茂權斬之。

translations.literal: On the day bingzi, Shu troops mounted the walls. Yang Sheng still led his men in fierce fighting until Wang Maoquan, overseeing officer of the Knives Corps, beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, Shu troops scaled the walls. Yang Sheng fought on until Wang Maoquan of the Knives Corps cut off his head.

sentences.zh: 獲彭州馬步使安師建，建欲使為將，師建泣謝曰：「師建誓與楊司徒同生死，不忍復戴日月，惟速死為惠。」

translations.literal: They captured An Shijian, Pengzhou horse-and-foot commissioner. Jian wished to make him a general. Shijian wept and declined: "Shijian swore to live and die with Minister Yang; I cannot bear to serve under the sun and moon again—only swift death would be a kindness."
translations.idiomatic: They took An Shijian, Pengzhou's horse-and-foot commissioner. Jian wanted him as a general. Shijian wept: "I swore to live and die with Minister Yang. I cannot serve another master—only let me die quickly."

sentences.zh: 再三諭之，不從，乃殺之，禮葬而祭之。

translations.literal: Jian urged him again and again; he would not comply, and so was killed, then buried and sacrificed to with full rites.
translations.idiomatic: Jian urged him repeatedly; when he refused, he was killed, then buried and honored with rites.

sentences.zh: 更趙章姓名曰王宗勉，王茂權名曰宗訓，又更王釗名曰宗謹，李綰姓曰王宗勉，王茂權名曰宗訓，又更王釗名曰宗謹，李綰姓名曰王宗綰。

translations.literal: Zhao Zhang's name was changed to Wang Zongmian; Wang Maoquan's to Wang Zongxun; Wang Zhao's to Wang Zongjin; and Li Wan's to Wang Zongwan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhang was renamed Wang Zongmian; Wang Maoquan, Wang Zongxun; Wang Zhao, Wang Zongjin; and Li Wan, Wang Zongwan.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，中書侍郎、同平章事鄭延昌罷為右僕射。

translations.literal: On the day xinmao, Zheng Yanchang, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Chief Minister, was removed and made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, Zheng Yanchang was dismissed from the chancellorship and made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 朱瑄、朱瑾求救於河東，李克用遣騎將安福順及弟福慶、福遷督精騎五百假道於魏，渡河應之。

translations.literal: Zhu Xuan and Zhu Jin begged Hedong for rescue. Li Keyong sent cavalry general An Fushun and his brothers Fuqing and Fuqian with five hundred elite horsemen to pass through Wei and cross the river to aid them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xuan and Zhu Jin begged Hedong for aid. Li Keyong sent An Fushun and his brothers with five hundred elite horse through Wei to cross the river and help.

sentences.zh: 武昌節度使杜洪攻黃州，楊行密遣行營都指揮使朱延壽等救之。

translations.literal: Du Hong, military governor of Wuchang, attacked Huangzhou. Yang Xingmi sent campaign commander Zhu Yanshou and others to rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: Du Hong of Wuchang attacked Huangzhou. Yang Xingmi sent Zhu Yanshou to relieve it.

sentences.zh: 六月，甲午，以宋州刺史張廷范為武寧節度使，從朱全忠之請也。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day jiawu, Zhang Tingfan, prefect of Songzhou, was appointed military governor of Wuning, acceding to Zhu Quanzhong's request.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jiawu, Zhang Tingfan of Songzhou was made Wuning governor at Zhu Quanzhong's request.

sentences.zh: 蘄州刺史馮敬章邀擊淮南軍，朱延壽攻蘄州，不克。

translations.literal: Feng Jingzhang, prefect of Qizhou, intercepted and attacked the Huainan army. Zhu Yanshou attacked Qizhou but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Jingzhang of Qizhou ambushed the Huainan army. Zhu Yanshou assaulted Qizhou but failed.

sentences.zh: 戊午，以翰林學士承旨、禮部尚書李谿同平章事；

translations.literal: On the day wuwu, Li Xi, Academician Expositor-in-Chief and Minister of Rites, was appointed Associate Chief Minister;
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, Li Xi, chief academician and Minister of Rites, was made Associate Chief Minister;

sentences.zh: 方宣制，水部郎中知制誥劉崇魯出班掠麻慟哭。

translations.literal: as the edict was being proclaimed, Liu Chonglu of the Water Ministry, drafting edicts, stepped from the ranks, seized the hemp band, and wailed.
translations.idiomatic: as the edict was read, Liu Chonglu of the Water Ministry seized the mourning band and wailed.

sentences.zh: 上召崇魯，問其故，對言：「谿奸邪，依附楊復恭、西門君遂，得在翰林，無相業，恐危社稷。」

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned Chonglu and asked the reason. He replied: "Xi is treacherous, clinging to Yang Fugong and Ximen Junsui to enter the Hanlin; he has no talent for governing and may endanger the realm."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor summoned Chonglu, who said: "Xi is wicked, rose through Yang Fugong and Ximen Junsui, has no talent for office, and may endanger the state."

sentences.zh: 谿竟罷為太子少傅。

translations.literal: Xi was in the end removed and made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was demoted to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 谿，鄜之孫也。

translations.literal: Xi was a grandson of Li Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was a grandson of Li Ye.

sentences.zh: 上師谿為文，崔昭緯恐谿為相，分己權，故使崇魯沮之。

translations.literal: The Emperor admired Xi's literary skill. Cui Zhaowei feared Xi as chancellor would divide his power and therefore had Chonglu obstruct him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor admired Xi's writing. Cui Zhaowei feared he would lose power and set Chonglu against him.

sentences.zh: 谿十表自訟，醜詆崇魯父符「受贓枉法，事覺自殺；

translations.literal: Xi memorialized ten times in his own defense, vilifying Chonglu's father Fu: "He took bribes and perverted the law; when exposed he killed himself;
translations.idiomatic: Xi memorialized ten times, attacking Chonglu's father Fu for taking bribes and killing himself when exposed;

sentences.zh: 弟崇望與楊復恭深交，崇魯庭拜田令孜，為朱玫作勸進表，乃雲臣交結內臣，何異抱贓唱賊！

translations.literal: his brother Chongwang was intimate with Yang Fugong; Chonglu bowed to Tian Lingzi in the courtyard and drafted Zhu Mei's petition urging enthronement—yet he says I associate with inner attendants; how is that different from embracing a thief and shouting 'thief'!
translations.idiomatic: his brother Chongwang was Yang Fugong's friend; Chonglu bowed to Tian Lingzi and wrote Zhu Mei's enthronement petition—yet he accuses me of consorting with eunuchs, like a thief crying thief!

sentences.zh: 且故事，絁巾慘帶，不入禁庭。

translations.literal: Moreover by precedent, coarse-cloth headbands and white mourning sashes do not enter the forbidden court.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, coarse mourning dress does not enter the palace.

sentences.zh: 臣果不才，崇魯自應上章論列，豈於正殿慟哭！

translations.literal: If your servant is truly without talent, Chonglu ought to memorialize on it—how could he wail in the main hall!
translations.idiomatic: If I am unfit, Chonglu should memorialize—not wail in the main hall!

sentences.zh: 為國不祥，無人臣禮，乞正其罪。」

translations.literal: It is ill-omened for the state and lacks the rites of a subject; I beg that his crime be rectified."
translations.idiomatic: It is an ill omen and breaches subject's rites; punish him."

sentences.zh: 詔停崇魯見任。

translations.literal: An edict suspended Chonglu from his current post.
translations.idiomatic: Chonglu was suspended from office.

sentences.zh: 谿猶上表不已，乞行誅竄，表數千言，詬詈無所不至。

translations.literal: Xi still memorialized without cease, begging execution or exile; his memorials ran to thousands of words with abuse of every kind.
translations.idiomatic: Xi kept memorializing, demanding Chonglu's death or exile in thousands of words of abuse.

sentences.zh: 李克用大破吐谷渾，殺赫連鐸，擒白義誠。

translations.literal: Li Keyong routed the Tuyuhun utterly, killed Helian Duo, and captured Bai Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong shattered the Tuyuhun, killed Helian Duo, and captured Bai Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，李茂貞遣兵攻閬州，撥之，楊復恭、楊守亮、楊守信帥其族黨犯圍走。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Li Maozhen sent troops to attack Langzhou and took it. Yang Fugong, Yang Shouliang, and Yang Shouxin led their clansmen in breaking the siege and fleeing.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, Li Maozhen took Langzhou. Yang Fugong, Shouliang, and Shouxin broke out with their kin.

sentences.zh: 禮部侍郎、同平章事鄭綮自以不合眾望，累表避位，詔以太子少保致仕；

translations.literal: Zheng Yin, Vice Minister of Rites and Associate Chief Minister, considered himself unworthy of public expectation and repeatedly memorialized to yield his post; an edict made him Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent in retirement;
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yin, finding himself unpopular, repeatedly asked to resign and was retired as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent;

sentences.zh: 以御史大夫徐彥若為中書侍郎兼吏部尚書、同平章事。

translations.literal: Xu Yanruo, Censor-in-Chief, was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat, concurrently Minister of Personnel, and Associate Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yanruo was made Vice Director of the Secretariat, Minister of Personnel, and Associate Chief Minister.

sentences.zh: 綿州刺史楊守厚卒，其將常再榮舉城降王建。

translations.literal: Yang Shouhou, prefect of Mianzhou, died; his general Chang Zairong surrendered the city to Wang Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shouhou of Mianzhou died; Chang Zairong surrendered the city to Wang Jian.

sentences.zh: 楊復恭、守亮、守信將自商山奔河東，至乾元，遇華州兵，獲之。

translations.literal: Yang Fugong, Shouliang, and Shouxin were about to flee from Shangshan to Hedong; reaching Qianyuan they met Huazhou troops and were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Fugong, Shouliang, and Shouxin fled toward Hedong via Shangshan; at Qianyuan Huazhou troops seized them.

sentences.zh: 八月，韓建獻於闕下，斬於獨柳。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Han Jian presented them at the palace gates; they were beheaded at Duliang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Han Jian presented them at court; they were beheaded at Duliang.

sentences.zh: 李茂貞獻復恭遺守亮書，訴致仕之由云：「承天門乃隋家舊業，大侄但積粟訓兵，勿貢獻。

translations.literal: Li Maozhen presented a letter Fugong had left Shouliang explaining his retirement: "Chengtian Gate was the Sui house's old foundation. Great-nephew, only store grain and train troops—do not send tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen presented Fugong's letter to Shouliang: "Chengtian Gate was the Sui legacy. Nephew, store grain and train troops—send no tribute.

sentences.zh: 吾於荊榛中立壽王，才得尊位，廢定策國老，有如此負心門生天子！」

translations.literal: I raised Emperor Shou among thorns and brambles; he had barely gained the throne when he cast aside the elder statesman who fixed the succession—such an ungrateful pupil-emperor!"
translations.idiomatic: I raised Emperor Shou from ruin; he had barely reigned when he cast aside the statesman who made him—such an ungrateful pupil-emperor!"

sentences.zh: 昭義節度使康君立詣晉陽謁李克用。

translations.literal: Kang Junli, military governor of Zhaoyi, came to Jinyang to pay respects to Li Keyong.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Junli of Zhaoyi came to Jinyang to see Li Keyong.

sentences.zh: 己未，克用會諸將飲博，酒酣，克用語及李存孝，流涕不已。

translations.literal: On the day jiwei, Keyong feasted and gambled with his generals. When drunk, he spoke of Li Cunxiao and wept without cease.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, Keyong drank and gambled with his generals. Drunk, he spoke of Li Cunxiao and wept endlessly.

sentences.zh: 君立素與李存信善，一言忤旨。

translations.literal: Junli had long been friendly with Li Cunxin; one remark offended.
translations.idiomatic: Junli was close to Li Cunxin; one remark gave offense.

sentences.zh: 克用撥劍斫之，囚於馬步司。

translations.literal: Keyong drew his sword and struck him, imprisoning him in the horse-and-foot office.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong drew his sword and struck him, imprisoning him in the horse-and-foot office.

sentences.zh: 九月，庚申朔，出之，君立已死。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the gengshen new moon, he was released—but Junli was already dead.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the gengshen new moon, he was released—Junli was already dead.

sentences.zh: 克用表雲州刺史薛志誠為昭義留後。

translations.literal: Keyong memorialized that Xue Zhicheng, prefect of Yunzhou, be acting regent of Zhaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong made Xue Zhicheng of Yunzhou acting regent of Zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丁酉，封皇子祤為棣王，禊為虔王，禋為沂王，禕為遂王。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the day dingyou, the princes Yi was enfeoffed as Prince of Di, Xi as Prince of Qian, Yin as Prince of Yi, and Wei as Prince of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on dingyou, Princes Yi, Xi, Yin, and Wei were enfeoffed as Di, Qian, Yi, and Sui.

sentences.zh: 劉仁恭數因蓋寓獻策於李克用，願得兵萬人取幽州。

translations.literal: Liu Rengong repeatedly through Gai Yu offered plans to Li Keyong, wishing ten thousand troops to take Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Through Gai Yu, Liu Rengong repeatedly offered Li Keyong plans to take Youzhou with ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 克用方攻邢州，分兵數千，欲納仁恭於幽州，不克。

translations.literal: Keyong was then attacking Xingzhou; he detached several thousand troops to install Rengong in Youzhou but failed.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong was besieging Xingzhou; he sent several thousand men to install Rengong in Youzhou but failed.

sentences.zh: 李匡籌益驕，數侵河東之境。

translations.literal: Li Kuangchou grew ever more arrogant and repeatedly raided Hedong territory.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kuangchou grew arrogant and repeatedly raided Hedong.

sentences.zh: 克用怒，十一月，大舉兵攻匡籌，撥武州，進圍新州。

translations.literal: Keyong was enraged. In the eleventh month he raised a great army against Kuangchou, took Wuzhou, and advanced to besiege Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Keyong in the eleventh month marched in force against Kuangchou, took Wuzhou, and besieged Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 以涇原留後張鐇為彰義節度使。

translations.literal: Zhang Zheng, acting commissioner of Jingyuan, was appointed military governor of Zhangyi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zheng of Jingyuan was made military governor of Zhangyi.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠遣使至泗州，使者陵慢刺史張諫，諫舉州降楊行密。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong sent envoys to Sizhou; the envoys treated prefect Zhang Jian with contempt, and Jian surrendered the whole prefecture to Yang Xingmi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong's envoys insulted Zhang Jian of Sizhou; Jian surrendered the prefecture to Yang Xingmi.

sentences.zh: 行密遣押牙唐令回持茶萬餘斤如汴宋貿易，全忠執令回，盡取其茶。

translations.literal: Xingmi sent adjutant Tang Linghui with more than ten thousand jin of tea to trade at Bian and Song; Quanzhong seized Linghui and took all the tea.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi sent Tang Linghui with ten thousand jin of tea to trade at Bian and Song; Quanzhong seized him and took all the tea.

sentences.zh: 揚、汴始有隙。

translations.literal: Yang and Bian thereby first developed a rift.
translations.idiomatic: Yangzhou and Bianzhou were now at odds.

sentences.zh: 十二月，李匡籌遣大將將步騎數萬救新州，李克用選精兵逆戰於段莊，大破之，斬首萬餘級，生擒將校三百人，以練絲斥之，徇於城下。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Li Kuangchou sent a great general with tens of thousands of foot and horse to relieve Xinzhou. Li Keyong chose elite troops to meet them at Duanzhuang and routed them utterly, beheading more than ten thousand and capturing three hundred officers alive; he had them bound with silk cords and paraded below the walls.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Kuangchou sent tens of thousands to relieve Xinzhou. Keyong met them at Duanzhuang, killed more than ten thousand, captured three hundred officers, bound them with silk, and paraded them below the walls.

sentences.zh: 是夕，新州降。

translations.literal: That evening Xinzhou surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: That night Xinzhou surrendered.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，進攻媯州。

translations.literal: On the day xinhai, he advanced to attack Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai he attacked Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 壬子，匡籌復發兵出居庸關，克用使精騎當其前以疲之，遣步將李存審自他道出其背夾擊之，幽州兵大敗，殺獲萬計。

translations.literal: On the day renzi, Kuangchou again sent troops out through Juyong Pass. Keyong used elite cavalry to block their front and wear them down, and sent foot commander Li Cunshen by another route to strike their rear in pincers; the Youzhou army was utterly defeated with kills and captures beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, Kuangchou marched out through Juyong Pass. Keyong tired them with elite horse in front and sent Li Cunshen around to strike their rear; the Youzhou army was shattered.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，李匡籌挈其族奔滄州，義昌節度使盧彥威利其輜重、妓妾，遣兵攻之於景城，殺之，盡俘其眾。

translations.literal: On the day jiayin, Li Kuangchou fled with his clan to Cangzhou. Lu Yanwei, military governor of Yichang, coveted his baggage train and concubines, sent troops to attack him at Jingcheng, killed him, and captured all his followers.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, Kuangchou fled to Cangzhou with his clan. Lu Yanwei of Yichang coveted his baggage and women, attacked him at Jingcheng, killed him, and took all his men.

sentences.zh: 存審本姓苻，宛丘人，克用養以為子。

translations.literal: Cunshen was originally surnamed Fu, a native of Wanqiu; Keyong raised him as a son.
translations.idiomatic: Cunshen was born Fu, from Wanqiu; Keyong raised him as a son.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，克用進軍幽州，其大將請降。

translations.literal: On the day bingchen, Keyong advanced on Youzhou; his great generals requested surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, Keyong marched on Youzhou; his generals surrendered.

sentences.zh: 匡籌素暗懦，初據軍府，兄匡威聞之，謂諸將曰：「兄失弟得，不出吾家，亦復何恨！

translations.literal: Kuangchou had always been dim and timid. When he first seized headquarters, his elder brother Kuangwei heard and said to the generals: "Elder brother loses, younger brother gains—it does not leave our house; what is there to regret!
translations.idiomatic: Kuangchou was dull and timid. When he seized command, Kuangwei said to his generals: "Brother loses, brother gains—it stays in the family; what regret is there!

sentences.zh: 但惜匡籌才短，不能保守，得及二年，幸矣。」

translations.literal: Only I pity Kuangchou's short talent—he cannot hold it. If he manages two years, that will be fortunate enough."
translations.idiomatic: Only Kuangchou lacks talent to hold it. Two years would be lucky."

sentences.zh: 加匡國節度使王行約檢校待中。

translations.literal: Wang Xingyue, military governor of Kuangguo, was given the additional title of Inspector Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xingyue of Kuangguo was made Inspector Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 吳討畏杜洪之逼，納印請代於楊行密，行密以先鋒指揮使瞿章權知黃州。

translations.literal: Wu Tao, fearing Du Hong's pressure, surrendered his seal and asked Yang Xingmi to replace him; Xingmi appointed vanguard commander Qu Zhang acting prefect of Huangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Tao, fearing Du Hong, surrendered his post; Xingmi made Qu Zhang acting prefect of Huangzhou.

sentences.zh: 是歲，黃連洞蠻二萬圍汀州，福建觀察使王潮遣其將李承勳將萬人擊之；

translations.literal: That year, twenty thousand barbarians of Huangliandong besieged Tingzhou. Wang Chao, Fujian observation commissioner, sent his general Li Chengxun with ten thousand to strike them;
translations.idiomatic: That year, twenty thousand Huangliandong tribesmen besieged Tingzhou. Wang Chao of Fujian sent Li Chengxun with ten thousand against them;

sentences.zh: 蠻解去，承勳追擊之，至漿水口，破之。

translations.literal: the barbarians dispersed; Chengxun pursued to Jiangshuikou and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: they fled; Chengxun pursued to Jiangshuikou and broke them.

sentences.zh: 閩地略定。

translations.literal: The Min region was largely settled.
translations.idiomatic: Min was largely pacified.

sentences.zh: 潮遣僚佐巡州縣，勸農桑，定租稅，交好鄰道，保境息民，閩人安之。

translations.literal: Chao sent aides to tour prefectures and counties, urging farming and sericulture, fixing rents and taxes, befriending neighboring circuits, keeping the borders secure and the people at rest—the people of Min were content.
translations.idiomatic: Chao sent officials to tour the counties, promote farming, fix taxes, befriend neighbors, and keep the peace—the people of Min were content.

sentences.zh: 封州刺史劉謙卒，子隱居喪於賀江，士民百餘人謀亂，隱一夕盡誅之。

translations.literal: Liu Qian, prefect of Fengzhou, died. His son Yin was in mourning at the He River when more than a hundred officials and people plotted disorder; Yin executed them all in one night.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qian of Fengzhou died. His son Yin, mourning at the He River, learned that over a hundred men plotted revolt and executed them all in one night.

sentences.zh: 嶺南節度使劉崇龜召補右都押牙兼賀水鎮使；

translations.literal: Liu Chonggui, military governor of Lingnan, summoned him to fill the post of Right Chief Adjutant and concurrently commissioner of Heshui Town;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chonggui of Lingnan summoned him as Right Chief Adjutant and Heshui Town commissioner;

sentences.zh: 未幾，表為封州刺史。

translations.literal: before long memorialized that he be prefect of Fengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: and soon had him made prefect of Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 義勝節度使董昌為政苛虐，於常賦之外，加斂數倍，以充貢獻及中外饋遺，每旬發一綱，金萬兩，銀五千鋋，越綾萬五千匹，他物稱是，用卒五百人，或遇雨雪風水違程，則皆死。

translations.literal: Dong Chang, military governor of Yisheng, governed with harsh cruelty. Beyond regular taxes he levied several times more to supply tribute and gifts within and without the court. Every ten days a convoy departed: ten thousand taels of gold, five thousand ingots of silver, fifteen thousand bolts of Yue silk, and other goods in proportion, using five hundred soldiers—if rain, snow, wind, or water delayed the schedule, all died.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Chang of Yisheng ruled with cruel greed. Beyond regular taxes he levied several times more for tribute and gifts. Every ten days a convoy went out: ten thousand taels of gold, five thousand ingots of silver, fifteen thousand bolts of Yue silk, and more, with five hundred soldiers—delay from weather meant death for all.

sentences.zh: 責奉為天下最，由是朝廷以為忠，寵命相繼，官至司徒、同平章事，爵隴西郡王。

translations.literal: His tribute levies were the heaviest under heaven; the court therefore deemed him loyal, heaped favors upon him in succession, and he rose to Grand Master, Associate Chief Minister, and Prince of Longxi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His levies were the heaviest in the realm; the court called him loyal, heaped honors on him, and he rose to Grand Master, Associate Chief Minister, and Prince of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 是建生祠於越州，制度悉如禹廟，命民間禱賽者，無得之禹廟，皆之生祠。

translations.literal: He thereupon built a living shrine in Yuezhou, its regulations all like the Temple of Yu, ordering that common people praying and offering sacrifice must not go to Yu's temple but all to his living shrine.
translations.idiomatic: He built a living shrine in Yuezhou modeled on Yu's temple and ordered worshippers to pray there instead of at Yu's temple.

sentences.zh: 昌求為越王，朝廷未之許，昌不悅曰：「朝廷欲負我矣，我累年貢獻無算而惜一越王邪！」

translations.literal: Chang requested to be King of Yue; the court did not grant it. Chang said discontentedly: "The court means to wrong me! I have sent tribute beyond counting for years—yet it grudges one title of King of Yue!
translations.idiomatic: Chang asked to be King of Yue; the court refused. Chang said angrily: "The court wrongs me! I have sent boundless tribute for years—yet grudges the title King of Yue!"

sentences.zh: 有諂之者曰：「王為越王，曷若為越帝。」

translations.literal: A flatterer said: "If Your Majesty is King of Yue, how is that not as good as Emperor of Yue!"
translations.idiomatic: A flatterer said: "King of Yue—why not Emperor of Yue!"

sentences.zh: 於是民間訛言時世將變，競相帥填門喧噪，請昌為帝。

translations.literal: Thereupon popular rumor said the age was about to change; people vied to crowd the gates in clamor, asking that Chang be emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Rumor spread that the age was changing; crowds clamored at his gates begging him to become emperor.

sentences.zh: 昌大喜，遣人謝之曰：「天時未至，時至我自為之。」

translations.literal: Chang was greatly pleased and sent someone to thank them: "Heaven's season has not yet come; when it comes I shall act myself."
translations.idiomatic: Chang was delighted and sent thanks: "Heaven's hour has not come; when it comes I shall act."

sentences.zh: 其僚佐吳瑤、都虞候李暢之等皆勸成之，吏民獻謠讖符瑞者不可勝紀，其始賞之以錢數百緡，既而獻者日多，稍減至五百、三百而已，昌曰：「讖云『兔子上金床』，此謂我也。

translations.literal: His staff Wu Yao, chief overseeing officer Li Changzhi, and others all urged him to complete it. Officials and people presented songs, prophecies, and auspicious signs beyond counting. At first he rewarded them with several hundred strings of cash; as presenters grew daily numerous, rewards gradually fell to five hundred, then three hundred. Chang said: "The prophecy says 'the rabbit mounts the golden bed'—that means me.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yao, Li Changzhi, and others urged him on. Officials and people brought prophecies and omens beyond count. At first he rewarded them with hundreds of strings of cash; as presenters multiplied, rewards fell to five hundred, then three hundred. Chang said: "The prophecy says 'the rabbit mounts the golden bed'—that is me.

sentences.zh: 我生太歲在卯，明年復在卯，二月卯日卯時，吾稱帝之秋也。」

translations.literal: I was born in a year of the mao branch; next year is mao again—the mao day and mao hour of the second month is the season when I shall proclaim myself emperor."
translations.idiomatic: I was born in a mao year; next year is mao again—the mao day and mao hour of the second month is when I shall proclaim myself emperor."
